e: 「中國」是東亞最大的國家。它的人口也是世界上第二多的國家。
q: ＿＿＿ is the largest country in East Asia（亞洲）. Its population（人口）is also the second largest country in the world.

e: 哇！你的公寓好大，而且從「陽臺」看出去的景色很棒。
q: Wow! Your apartment is so big, and the view from the ＿＿＿ is great.

e: Carol 每隔幾天就會去拜訪她年長的「鄰居」，確認他平安無恙，因為那位可憐的老人沒有任何親戚在身邊照顧他。
q: Carol visits her elderly ＿＿＿ every few days to make sure that he’s all right because the poor old man doesn’t have any relatives（親戚）around to take care of him.

e: 在美國的某些地方，在自家前的「院子」種植蔬菜而非草地是違法的。
q: In some parts of the USA, it is against the law（法律）to grow vegetables instead of grass in one’s front ＿＿＿.

e: 與螫一次就可能會喪命的工蜂不一樣，每一隻「螞蟻」都可以螫或咬許多次。
q: Unlike worker honeybees, which may lose their lives after they sting（螫）once, each ＿＿＿ can sting or bite several times.

e: 甚至連待在這個產業很久的 Cathy 也難「看出」錯誤，所以不要對你自己這麼嚴格了。
q: Even Cathy, who has been in the business for a long time, has trouble ＿＿＿ the errors, so don’t be so hard on yourself.

e: 根據這項研究，這個國家大部分的青少年依靠網路作為他們搜尋資料的主要「資訊來源」。
q: According to（根據）the study, most of the teenagers in this country rely on（依靠）the Internet as their main ＿＿＿ of information.

e: 世界上有那麼多公司，我們應該做什麼讓我們的公司成為對顧客來說是「可靠的」名字？
q: With so many businesses out there in the world, what should we do to make our company a ＿＿＿ name for customers?

e: 你看！我在網路上找到了一個關於健康飲食的「網站」。它的內容也包含了一些關於如何以健康的方式減重的資訊。
q: Look! I found a(n) ＿＿＿ about healthy diets（飲食） on the Internet. It also contains（包含）some information about how to lose weight in a healthy way.

e: 如果 Bob 持續因為他做出的糟糕決定而被獎賞，那麼他將永遠不會知道自己的做法有「錯誤」。
q: Bob will never see the ＿＿＿ of his ways if he keeps being rewarded（獎賞）for the bad decisions（決定）he’s made.

e: 我的老闆要我把這份檔案列印出來，並在明天早上把「複本」放在她的桌上。
q: My boss asked me to print（列印）the file out and put the ＿＿＿ on her table tomorrow morning.

e: 那個小女孩被巨大的風箏捲到空中的新聞登上了所有報紙的「標題」。
q: The news that a little girl was sent flying into the air by a giant kite hit the ＿＿＿ across all the newspapers.

e: 不要在博物館內「抽菸」。事實上，你不可以在任何公共場所做那件事。
q: ＿＿＿ isn’t allowed inside the museum. In fact, you can’t do that in any public places.

e: Mia：Ann 沒有說「實話」。 Dan：你怎麼知道？ Mia：她每次說謊都會很大聲。
q:
Mia：Ann didn’t tell the ＿＿＿.
Dan：How did you know?
Mia：Every time she lies, she talks loudly.

e: 在數學課上，我們學到了利用這些工具畫出和測量不同的「角度」。很有趣。
q: In the math class, we learned to draw and measure（測量）different ______ with these tools. It was interesting.

e: A：那座美術館離這裡不「遠」。 B：既然那樣的話，我們何不走路去那裡？
q:
A：The art museum is not ______ from here.
B：In that case, why don’t we walk there?

e: 你對 Lily 說的話有點「太過頭」。我認為你應該要跟她道歉。
q: What you said to Lily was a bit（有點）______. I think you should say sorry to her.

e: 「長椅」上的油漆未乾。請不要坐在上面。
q: The paint（油漆）on the ______ is still wet. Don’t sit on it.

e: Dan 出國時總是背一個大的後背包。那樣「當他在旅行時」，他的雙手可以保持空閒。連接詞用 when 表「當……時」。
q: Dan always carries a big backpack（後背包）when he goes abroad. That keeps his hands free ＿＿＿ he travels（旅行）.

e: 你為什麼拿走那筆錢？「只要」你跟我說真相，我就會原諒你。連接詞用 as long as 表「只要……就……」。
q: Why did you take away the money? ＿＿＿ you tell me the truth, I will forgive（原諒）you.

e: 「我一到火車站，火車就開走了」，所以我不得不搭公車到高雄。連接詞用 as soon as 表「一……就……」。
q: The train left ＿＿＿ I arrived at the train station, so I had no choice but to take a bus to Kaohsiung.

e: 當 John 把燈關掉時，Betty 正在泡澡。while 後方不常接瞬間動作，故用連接詞 when。且此句在敘述過去的事件，故時態用過去式。
q: Betty ＿＿＿ a bath ＿＿＿ John turned off the light. She was scared and cried out for help.

e: 當 as long as 連接兩個表未來的子句時，as long as 引導的子句要用現在簡單式代替未來式。
q: As long as you ＿＿＿ me the truth, you won’t be in trouble.

e: as soon as 用於連接過去發生的兩件事時，其引導的子句用過去簡單式。
q: As soon as Jay ＿＿＿ a bite of the stinky tofu（臭豆腐）, he fell in love with it.

e: 「當 Jacky 與 Steve 讀國中時」，他們認識了。連接詞用 while 表「當……時」。
q: Jacky and Steve met ______ they were in junior high school. They’ve been good friends since then.

e: 「當你到家時」，Joanna 打掃完房子了嗎？連接詞用 when 表「當……時」。
q:
A：Did Joanna finish cleaning the house ＿＿＿ you arrived home?
B：No, she didn’t. She was mopping the floor then.

e: 連接詞 as soon as 用於連接過去發生的兩件事時，其所引導的子句用過去簡單式。
q: The man ran over to save the little girl as soon as he ＿＿＿ that a big dog was about to bite her.

e: while 連接兩個動作時，持續的動作用進行式，突發的瞬間動作用簡單式。且由 happened 可知，此句在敘述過去發生的事，故用過去進行式。
q: While we ＿＿＿ basketball in the gym, the earthquake happened. We covered our heads and found a safe place to hide right away.

e: 當 if 連接兩個表未來的子句時，if 引導的子句要用現在簡單式代替未來式。
q: If Judy ＿＿＿ the test again, her parents won’t allow her to play video games.

e: A：為什麼昨晚你沒有接我電話？我打電話給你好幾次。 B：「當你打電話給我時」，我正在淋浴，「所以」我沒有聽到電話鈴響。第一格用連接詞 when，第二格用連接詞 so。
q:
A：Why didn’t you answer my calls last night? I called you several times.
B：I was taking a shower ＿＿＿ you called, ＿＿＿ I didn’t hear the phone ring（響起鈴聲）.

e: A：你通常做什麼運動？你打網球或羽球嗎？ B：不，我不打。我通常會去公園慢跑，「因為」慢跑幫助我頭腦清醒並維持身形。連接詞用 because。
q:
A：What exercise do you usually do? Do you play tennis or badminton?
B：No, I don’t. I usually go jogging in the park ＿＿＿ it helps clear my mind and stay in shape.

e: Jack「被他的科學老師要求」做一份關於昆蟲的報告，用被動語態 was asked。在他做研究「之後」，他發現瓢蟲一生中會吃超過五千隻昆蟲。連接詞用 After。
q: Jack ＿＿＿ to do a report about insects by his science teacher. ＿＿＿ he did some research（研究）, he found that a ladybird（瓢蟲）might eat more than 5,000 insects in its lifetime.

e: as soon as 連接兩件過去的事情時，其所引導的子句用過去簡單式。
q: My pet cat ran up to me as soon as I ＿＿＿ the door.

e: as soon as 用來連接兩個幾乎同時發生的動作，而 got to his office 為瞬間動作，故連接詞不可用 while。
q: I called Leo ＿＿＿ I got to his office. However, he didn’t answer my calls, and no one knew where he was.

e: as long as 連接兩個表未來的子句時，as long as 引導的子句要用現在簡單式代替未來式。
q: As long as Linda ＿＿＿ better from her bad cold, she’ll start to train for the sporting event.

e: 「當我正在睡覺時」，Mike 帶了晚餐回家。連接詞用 While。「在我起床之後」，我們一起看電視並吃晚餐。連接詞用 After。
q: ＿＿＿ I was sleeping, Mike brought dinner home. ＿＿＿ I got up, we watched TV and had dinner together.

e: as long as 連接表未來的兩個子句時，其引導的子句要以現在簡單式代替未來式。
q: As long as it ＿＿＿ this weekend, we will watch soccer games on TV at home.

e: 「當 Teddy 的朋友看到他時」，他正在餵他的狗。而 saw 為瞬間動作，故連接詞不可用 while，須使用 when。
q: Teddy was feeding his dog ＿＿＿ his friends saw him. They said hi to him and played with his dog for a while.

e: 「雖然」我擦了這面窗戶好幾次，但是它仍然很髒。你知道我該拿它怎麼辦嗎？連接詞用 though。
q: The window is still dirty ＿＿＿ I cleaned it several times. Do you know what I can do with it?

e: 「雖然」Ed 不富有，Jill 仍然嫁給他。她相信他就是那個會帶給她快樂的人。
q: ＿＿＿ Ed wasn’t rich, Jill still married him. She believed ＿＿＿ he was the one who could bring her happiness（快樂）.

e: 那位盲人要求 Karen 協助他過馬路，「因為」那時交通繁忙。連接詞用 because。
q: The blind man asked Karen to help him cross the road ＿＿＿ the traffic（交通）was heavy then.

e: 「雖然」Chapman 老師已經解釋這場比賽的規則很多遍，「但是」我仍然無法理解。although 與 but 不可同時出現在同一個句子。
q: ＿＿＿ Ms. Chapman has explained the rules of the game many times, ＿＿＿ I still don’t understand them.

e: as long as 連接兩個表未來的子句時，主要子句應使用未來式，而 as long as 連接的子句應使用現在簡單式代替未來式。
q: You ＿＿＿ better soon as long as you ＿＿＿ your medicine on time.

e: 「雖然」Meg 放學後覺得很累，但是她一到家，她媽媽就要她打掃她的房間。連接詞用 Though。
q: ＿＿＿ Meg felt tired after school, her mother asked her to clean up her room as soon as she ＿＿＿ home.

e: as… as… 表示「如同……一樣地……」。而此處須使用副詞 well 修飾前方動詞 sing。「只要」你努力，你將讓你的夢想成真。連接詞用 as long as 表「只要……就……」。
q:
Louis：Ed Sheeran is my favorite singer. I want to sing ＿＿＿ he does.
Ms. Lin：＿＿＿ you work hard, you will make your dream come true.
o: as well as; As long as
as well as; As soon as

e: as long as 連接兩個表未來的子句時，其引導的子句要用現在簡單式代替未來式。
q: We can use instant（即時的）messaging apps to make free phone calls and send messages to each other as long as the Internet ＿＿＿.

e: 「當我打開門時」，Terry 正在玩電玩遊戲。連接詞用 when。而 notice 為感官動詞，後接的動詞須是原形動詞或現在分詞（V-ing）。
q: Terry was playing the video games ＿＿＿ I opened the door. He was so focused（專注的）on the games, so he didn’t even notice me ＿＿＿ beside him.

e: B 回應「只要」車子與網路連接，Devin 就可以從他的辦公室控制它。連接詞用 as long as 表「只要……就……」。
q:
A：Everyone is talking about Devin’s new car. What’s special about it?
B：＿＿＿ it is connected（連接的）to the Internet, he can control（控制）it from his office.

e: Tim 一沒有車開過來就快速地跑到馬路的另一邊。連接詞用 as soon as 表「一……就……」。
q: Tim ran quickly to the other side ______ there were no cars coming.

e: 由 Tina 的回應可知，Judy 是在詢問 Tom 每次都能快速地完成他的回家作業的「原因」，故疑問詞用 Why。而 Tina 回覆因為「只要」Tom 完成他的回家作業，他就可以玩電腦遊戲。連接詞用 as long as 表「只要……就……」。
q:
Judy：＿＿＿ can Tom finish his homework so quickly every time?
Tina：Because he can play computer games ＿＿＿ he finishes his homework. Therefore, he always does his homework first after school.

e: 修飾動詞要用副詞，故第一格填 well。當 as long as 連接兩個表未來的子句時，as long as 引導的子句要用現在簡單式代替未來式。
q:
A：To be honest, I don’t think I can ever speak Japanese（日文）＿＿＿.
B：Hey, don’t give up! You will be good at it as long as you ______ practicing it.

e: 由後句文意可知，林老師班級的學生今天「即將考」數學考試，動詞用未來式。林老師班級的學生們「只要」過去幾週在課堂上有注意聽林老師的講課內容，這次數學考試他們就可以考好。連接詞用 as long as。
q: The students in Ms. Lin’s class ＿＿＿ a math test today. They can do well on it ＿＿＿ they have paid attention（注意）to what Ms. Lin said in class over the past few weeks.
o: are going to take; as long as

e: 在那個強颱襲擊那座城市「之後」，許多人失去了他們的家及家人。連接詞用 After。
q: ＿＿＿ the strong typhoon hit the city, many people lost their homes and families.

e: Amy 的回應為那場棒球比賽一結束，Josh 就會做家事。連接詞用 as soon as 表「一……就……」。而當 as soon as 連接兩個表未來的子句時，as soon as 引導的子句要用現在簡單式代替未來式。
q:
Dad：What is Josh doing? It’s his turn to do the housework today.
Amy：He is watching a baseball game on TV. He will do the housework ＿＿＿ the game ＿＿＿ over.

e: 「關於……」的介系詞用 about。而由 A 問「為什麼 Bill 今天沒有來上學」可知，B 是回答「因為」Bill 重感冒。連接詞用 Because。
q:
A：Why didn’t Bill come to school today? I was going to borrow（借入）a book ＿＿＿ plants from him.
B：＿＿＿ he caught a bad cold.

e: 強調兩件事持續在同一時間發生，通常用 while 連接兩個過去進行式的句子。
q: Helen was playing video games ＿＿＿ her brother was doing homework in his room.

e: 由 A 問「為什麼 Mandy 瞇著眼睛看黑板」可知，B 是回覆「因為」她沒戴眼鏡，黑板上的字對她來說不清楚，連接詞用 Because。
q:
A：Why is Mandy squinting（瞇著眼看）at the blackboard（黑板）?
B：＿＿＿ she isn’t wearing her glasses, and the words on the blackboard are not clear to her.

e: 「當」Danny 昨天晚上在公園慢跑時，他意外地弄傷了他的腿，「所以」他不得不放棄那場跑步比賽。because 與 so 不可同時出現在同一個句子。
q: ＿＿＿ Danny broke his leg by accident ＿＿＿ he was jogging in the park yesterday evening, ＿＿＿ he has no choice but to give up the running race.

e: 「雖然」那位科學家失敗了許多次，但是他依然持續進行他的實驗。連接詞用 although。
q:
John：The scientist（科學家）keeps carrying out the experiment（實驗）＿＿＿ he has failed many times.
Kate：Yeah. He keeps working and never gives up.

e: 「直到」Jason 有足夠的錢之前，他都不會購買那支他已經想要很久的手錶。連接詞用 until。
q: Jason will not buy the watch that he has wanted for a long time ＿＿＿ he has enough money for it. He will never borrow（借入）money for something he can’t afford（負擔）.

e: while 連接兩個動作時，持續的動作用進行式，突發的瞬間動作用簡單式。
q: I ＿＿＿ a loud noise outside my room while I ＿＿＿ a comic book last night. Then I checked every corner of my house, but I didn’t find anything strange.

e: while 連接兩個動作時，持續的動作用進行式，突發的瞬間動作用簡單式。saw 後為 that 引導的名詞子句，而過去時間中正在發生的事情須用過去進行式表示。
q: While I ＿＿＿ past Emma’s house, I saw she ＿＿＿ the flowers in the yard. She really spent a lot of time taking care of the flowers.

e: 「如果」你去造訪 Joe 的房子，你將會發現「一些有趣的東西」。連接詞用 if。而用形容詞修飾複合代名詞 something 時，形容詞須放在 something 的後面。
q: You will find ＿＿＿ ＿＿＿ you visit Joe’s house. It’s the most special house that I’ve ever seen.

e: while 連接兩個動作時，持續的動作用進行式，突發的瞬間動作用簡單式。
q: We ＿＿＿ a giant black bear while we ＿＿＿ in the mountains yesterday. It was really scary.

e: 連接兩件幾乎同時發生的事件，連接詞用 when。而當 when 連接兩個動作時，持續的動作用進行式，突發的瞬間動作用簡單式。
q:
Lynn：Stacy seemed（似乎）busy yesterday. I couldn’t reach her in the afternoon.
Bonnie：I couldn’t, either. She later told me that she ＿＿＿ dinner ＿＿＿ you called her.

e: 「如果」Jessie 無法在她下班前完成她的工作，她將無法及時趕上約會。連接詞用 If。
q: ＿＿＿ Jessie can’t finish her work before she gets off work, she won’t be able to make it to the date with her boyfriend.

e: before 連接兩個表未來的子句時，其引導的子句要用現在簡單式代替未來式。
q: The sky is dark. I want to get home before it ＿＿＿.

e: look 當連綴動詞表「看起來」時，後面須接形容詞或「like＋名詞」。而 B 回覆，林老師要 Josh 在離開教室「之前」，把所有的電燈都關掉，但是他忘記這件事了。連接詞用 before。
q:
A：What happened to Ms. Lin? She ＿＿＿ so mad.
B：She asked Josh to turn off all the lights ＿＿＿ he left the classroom yesterday, but he forgot to do it.

e: A：我不知道該如何用我的智慧型手機上網。 B：「你在和我開玩笑嗎？」連我五歲的兒子都知道怎麼做。 A：我是說真的。你可以教我嗎？
q:
A：I don’t know how to surf the Internet on my smartphone.
B：＿＿＿ Even my five-year-old son knows how to do that.
A：I really mean it. Could you teach me?
o: What a lazy guy you are!
You may get into trouble because of that.

g: 連接詞 as soon as、as long as
e: Kevin 工作忙碌，且常常加班。然而，「只要他工作提早結束」，他就會回家吃晚餐。
q: Kevin is busy with his work, and he often works overtime. However, he comes home for dinner ______.
o: while he is in his office
as soon as he reaches his family
as long as he finishes work early
because work is an important part of his life

e: 我爺爺真地喜歡他新的智慧型手機。有了它，「他可以很快地得知很多事情」。生活對他來說變得簡單許多。
q: My grandpa really likes his new smartphone. With it, ______. Life is much easier for him.
o: he will never be tricked by fake news
he is able to trick people around him for fun
he can learn about many things in a second
he won’t be attacked by foreigners anymore

e: George：為什麼 Mark 去了警察局？他發生了什麼事？ Michelle：他去那裡向警方做筆錄，因為「他昨晚被一個壞人攻擊」。
q:
George：Why did Mark go to the police station? What happened to him?
Michelle：He went there to give a statement（做筆錄）to the police because ＿＿＿.
o: the police found fire ants in his garden
he thought the news report was so true
his neighbor saw bees in his house
he was attacked by a bad guy last night

e: A：你到家的時候 Jane 正在睡覺嗎？ B：對啊，而「當我在擺設餐桌時」，她起床了。
q:
A：Was Jane sleeping when you got home?
B：Yes, and she got up ＿＿＿.

She does that when we change classes at school, and she doesn’t even take her eyes off it to walk up and down the stairs. Also, when we’re out, she can’t even put it down for a second to cross the street. This really scares me __1.__ she had some close calls before. She almost got run over by a car a few times. I’ve tried many times to tell her how dangerous it is, but she wouldn’t listen to me. She doesn’t think it’s a big deal because nothing bad __2.__ to her yet. What can I do to save my friend?

------------------------------------------------------
Dear Outsmartphoned,
__3.__ It’s too bad more of today’s young people aren’t like you. As for trying to save your friend, here are some things you can do. First, __4.__, ask her to put her phone down. If she doesn’t, you can ask her if she would rather hang out with her phone than you. Then, you can show her the videos that I’ve attached to the e-mail. She can watch what happened to people just like her. Sometimes seeing something with your own eyes will wake you up and help you see the error of your ways.

If a person you know asks you to do something, can they trust you to do it correctly? __1.__, would you admit your mistake instead of making excuses or pointing the finger at others? If your answer is no to one or both of these questions, then you are probably not a very responsible person.

That means not taking on more than you can deal with, __3.__, or not doing a poor job just because you want to get it done quickly and move on to better and more interesting activities.
Being responsible for your actions shows others that you can be trusted and also wins you respect. This in turn builds on your belief in yourself, __4.__ helps you get better, stand on your own two feet, and take control of your own life.

Since then, modern toilet paper __3.__ a long way. Today, it’s made in a lot of different colors and smells. p:
You have heard of eSports, haven’t you? For those that have, do you think they are real sports? For those that haven’t, eSports is short for electronic sports, and they are competitions that use video games instead of traditional ball games. These kinds of competitions have been around since the late 1970s.
At the start, how to be a good player was decided by how many points he or she was able to get during play, and the best players were the ones with the highest scores. As soon as the style of game play changed to fighting games, the way of deciding the winners also changed. The best players were the ones who beat or killed their opponents. It didn’t matter if the games were one-on-one, two-on-two, or more.
eSports became really popular as soon as the Internet grew in size and speed. The place which experienced that the most was South Korea. There, video games were more than something fun and interesting that was played to pass the time. They became real sports for the body and the mind, and people could actually make money while they were playing them. South Koreans couldn’t get enough of eSports, and they were even shown on TV all day and all night long. Soon, eSports were catching on in China and other parts of Asia. p:
Everyone loves watching movies. We enjoy them in movie theaters of all shapes and sizes as well as in our own comfortable homes. It’s also quite common for us to have yummy snacks like popcorn while we are watching the stories play out on our screens.
Not all movies are created the same, though. Some of them never make it to theaters even though they have wonderful stories. On the other hand, some of them are big hits at theaters even though their stories are nothing special. So, what is it that makes a movie successful? For the people that are in the movie business, the money that the movie makes at the box office is what makes it successful. They don’t look at the money that the movie brings in from its home videos, being shown on TV, or tie-in products because the sales information for those aren’t always easily gotten.
War movies, musicals, and historical dramas have long been the most popular kinds. However, those went out the window as soon as franchise movies came along in the 21st century. The kinds that have really won people’s hearts are the ones with superheroes from Marvel Comics. The Star Wars, Harry Potter, and Jurassic Park franchises also have lots of fans. Even so, if you adjust the box office sales for inflation, you’ll see that the old movies still stand up to what the modern world has given us.

p:
Fake news is on the rise, so it’s not surprising that it has made a lot of headlines recently. The stories are full of false information as well as information that leads people to think, believe, and do wrong things. They are seen by some to be funny and nothing terrible. However, they are seen by others to be powerful enough to cause change and cause people to take sides.
This leads to the question—what were Facebook, Twitter, and other Internet companies doing while fake news was being spread all over the Internet? What’s more, what were governments doing while big TV news stations were spreading fake news themselves? We know now that some action was taken. However, it wasn’t enough to stop people from getting confused about simple and easily checked facts.
As long as more isn’t done to stop the spread of fake news, the problem won’t go away. So, who is responsible for fighting fake news? Internet companies like Facebook believe that they are partly responsible for doing that. They have started using new tools that will help stop the quick spread of fake news. Even so, they still have a hard time staying ahead of people who try to cause problems. As soon as they block or take one down, another pops up to take its place. The Internet companies also believe that more should be done by governments to keep an eye on the information that the public can get their hands on.

e: 威廉‧莎士比亞被「廣泛地」認為是最偉大的作家之一。《羅密歐與茱麗葉》及《哈姆雷特》是他其中兩部最著名的作品。
q: William Shakespeare is ＿＿＿ regarded（被……認為）as one of the greatest writers. Romeo and Juliet and Hamlet are two of his most famous works.

e: 我上個禮拜加入羽球隊。現在，我是隊上的新「成員」。
q: I joined the badminton team last week. Now, I am a fresh _______ of the team.

e: 貓喜歡「狩獵」老鼠和鳥眾所皆知。事實上，牠們也是昆蟲殺手。
q: It is known that cats like to ＿＿＿ mice and birds. In fact, they are also insect killers（昆蟲殺手）.

e: 兒子：爸爸，為什麼「前方的」車子沒有在移動？ 爸爸：因為有棵樹倒下並堵住道路。
q:
Son：Dad, why aren’t the cars ＿＿＿ of us moving?
Dad：Because a tree fell down and blocked the road.

e: 我的祖父母希望看到我結婚。令人遺憾地，他們「兩個都沒」能活那麼久。
q: My grandparents hoped to see me get married. Sadly, ______ of them lived that long.

e: George：感謝你的造訪。你帶給我們很多「歡樂」。 Monica：不客氣。跟你們在一起是我的榮幸。
q:
George：Thank you for your visit. You brought a lot of ＿＿＿ to us.
Monica：You’re welcome. It’s my pleasure to be with you.

e: 令人驚訝的是，Jack 的女朋友是我的遠房「親戚」之一。我們已經有好長一段時間沒見到彼此。
q: It is surprising that Jack’s girlfriend is a distant（遠房的）＿＿＿ of mine. We haven’t seen each other for a long time.

e: 在西方文化中，詢問他人賺多少錢是不「禮貌的」。甚至跟朋友談到錢都是很私人的事。
q: In Western（西方的）culture, it’s not ______ to ask people how much they make. It’s very personal（私人的）to talk about money, even with friends.

e: Joseph 去年開始在日本工作。然而，他的妻子跟小孩都仍住在臺灣。所以，他起初到日本時感到很「孤單」。
q: Joseph started working in Japan last year. However, his wife and kids still live in Taiwan. So, he felt very ＿＿＿ when he first got there.

e: 做運動是我的「嗜好」。我每天都做。它幫助我感到開心並忘掉所有煩心的事。
q: Playing sports is my ＿＿＿. I do it every day. It helps me feel happy and forget all the bad things.

e: 你傷了 Kate 的「感情」。你最好現在立刻去跟她道歉。
q: You hurt Kate’s ＿＿＿. You’d better（最好）say sorry to her right now.

e: Jessica 很安靜又「害羞」。她很少跟她班上的男生說話。
q: Jessica is very quiet and ＿＿＿. She seldom talks to the boys in her class.

e: 臺北市的「交通」很繁忙。你最好別開車去上班，因為會花你很多時間。
q: The ＿＿＿ in Taipei City is heavy. You’d better（最好）not drive to work because it will take you a lot of time.

e: 新年快到了。我媽媽要求我「整理」我自己的房間跟拖地板。
q: The New Year is coming. My mom asked me to ＿＿＿ up my own room and mop the floor.

e: Todd：這是怎麼發生的？ Joyce：球「滾到」街上，Peter 沒有看就跑出去了。
q:
Todd：How did this happen?
Joyce：The ball ＿＿＿ the street, and Peter ran out without looking.

e: Ivy：這場表演的門票是新臺幣 500 元。 Tim：哎喲。我的錢包裡只有新臺幣 400 元。請「借」我一些錢。
q:
Ivy：The ticket to the show is NT$500.
Tim：Oops. There is only NT$400 in my wallet. Please ＿＿＿ me some money.

e: 由圖可知，Ted 昨天跟 Alex「借」了一本書。
q: Look at the picture. Ted ______ a book from Alex yesterday.

e: 臺灣人通常去寺廟向「神」祈求。這是臺灣文化的一部分。
q: Taiwanese usually go to temple to pray to the ＿＿＿. It’s a part of Taiwanese culture（文化）.

e: Terry 把他的「傘」留在公車上。難怪他在雨中全身淋濕。
q: Terry left his ＿＿＿ on the bus. No wonder he got all wet in the rain.

e: 我在雨中騎機車時全身淋濕。當我到家時，我媽媽給了我一條「毛巾」擦乾身體。
q: I got all wet when I was riding my scooter in the rain. My mom gave me a(n) ＿＿＿ to dry my body when I got home.

e: Amy：你為什麼沒有來電影院，Sam？電影開始了。 Sam：我很抱歉不能去了，因為我的車深陷於「泥土」中。
q:
Amy：Why didn’t you come to the movie theater, Sam? The movie is on.
Sam：I’m sorry I can’t go because my car is stuck（卡住的）in the heavy ＿＿＿.

e: 由圖可知，那位男子對那對母女來說是「陌生人」。
q: Look at the picture. The man is a ＿＿＿ to the mother and the daughter.

e: 你「貶低」身邊的人時一點也不好玩。你應該總是尊重他人。
q: It’s not funny at all when you ＿＿＿ people around you. You should always respect（尊重）others.

e: Cathy 不吃任何肉。可知她「既不」喜歡豬肉，「也不」喜歡牛肉。用 neither... nor...。
q: Cathy likes ＿＿＿ pork ＿＿＿ beef. She doesn’t eat any meat.

e: Jenny 跟 Lisa「兩人都不」是我的朋友，用 Neither... nor...；我從未跟她們「任一個」講過話，用 either of them。
q: ＿＿＿ Jenny ＿＿＿ Lisa is my friend. I’ve never talked to ＿＿＿ of them.

e: 這臺筆記型電腦「既不」輕「也不」便宜。我不會買它。用 neither... nor...。
q: This notebook computer is ＿＿＿ light ＿＿＿ cheap. I won’t get it.

e: 房子很乾淨。院子跟陽臺「都不」需要打掃。用 Neither... nor...。
q: The house is very tidy. ＿＿＿ the yard ＿＿＿ the balcony ＿＿＿ to be cleaned.

e: Johnson 醫生想要他女兒長大時「不是」當醫生，「就是」當護理師，這麼一來，他有一天能和女兒在同一家醫院工作。用 either... or...。
q: Dr. Johnson wants his daughter to be ＿＿＿ a doctor ＿＿＿ a nurse when she grows up. That way, he could work in the same hospital with her someday.

e: 由副詞 yet 可知，應使用完成式，且應為否定句；我還沒完成我的工作。我「既不」能去健身房，「也不」能跟你去購物。用 neither... nor...。
q: I ＿＿＿ my work yet. I can ＿＿＿ go to the gym ＿＿＿ go shopping with you.
o: have finished; not only; but also

e: 選其中一種運動，用 either... or...。
q:
Ruth：Jimmy, we can play ＿＿＿ basketball ＿＿＿ badminton after school today. Which do you prefer（偏好）?
Jimmy：Basketball.

e: 用 either... or... 連接主詞時，由 or 後面的主詞決定動詞，I 為第一人稱，故動詞用 am 或 was。
q: Either you or I ＿＿＿ right about the answer to the question.

e: 用 either... or... 連接主詞時，由 or 後面的主詞決定動詞；動名詞片語視為單數主詞，故接單數 be 動詞。
q: Either playing video games or going to the movies ＿＿＿ a lot of fun.

e: Ben 認為長椅上的手機「不是」屬於那位男士的，「就是」那位女士的。Liz 看到螢幕上有那位女士的照片，故推測手機一定是那位女士的。用 either... or...。
q:
Liz：Hey! There is a smartphone on the bench.
Ben：It may belong to ＿＿＿ the man ＿＿＿ the woman.
Liz：Look! The woman’s picture is on the screen. It must be the woman’s.

e: 否定倒裝句用 neither，且時態與動詞須與主要子句一致，主要子句為現在完成式。
q: Laura hasn’t finished her homework, and ＿＿＿ her brothers. So, they can’t play video games.

e: 表示「也不……」用否定詞 either，動詞與前句動詞 she is not in the race 一致，應用 be 動詞。
q:
A：Which runner is Cara?
B：Well, she is not in the race.
A：How about John?
B：He ＿＿＿, ＿＿＿.

e: 因前句為含現在式一般動詞的肯定句，其肯定附和句為「主詞＋do / does, too」或「so＋do / does＋主詞」。
q: Most students hate tests and homework. However, doing homework helps them learn well, and ______.

e: 倒裝句的動詞和時態須和主要子句的動詞一致，主要子句的動詞為過去式一般動詞，故倒裝句動詞為過去式助動詞，且由後句可判斷應為肯定句。
q: Brian bought a ticket for BTS’s concert（演唱會）, and ＿＿＿ Ted. They are both BTS’s fans.

e: 表示「也不……」用否定詞加 either。
q:
Mary：I can’t drive. Can you give me a ride to the supermarket?
Anderson：I ＿＿＿, ＿＿＿. Sorry.

e: neither 為否定副詞，因此附和句中的助動詞不須再加否定詞。
q:
A：I can’t ride a scooter.
B：＿＿＿ Let’s take a taxi to the theater together.

e: 句意表示「如此……以致於……」，且空格後為形容詞，故應使用副詞 so 修飾；前句時態為過去式，故後句亦應為過去式。
q: Joey was ＿＿＿ thirsty that he ＿＿＿ up a bottle of water in ten seconds.

e: 否定倒裝句用 neither，時態與動詞須與主要子句一致。
q:
Doris：Jack is not afraid of cockroaches（蟑螂）. I saw him drive a cockroach away in the kitchen yesterday.
Amy：＿＿＿ Ken. He looked calm（冷靜的）when he saw the cockroach.

e: 先行詞 the girl 為人，以 who / that 引導形容詞子句修飾先行詞，且關係代名詞當主格時不得省略；由前方動詞 Look 可知此處動詞應使用現在式。
q:
Joe：Will Mary come to the party?
Kate：Sure. Look! The girl ＿＿＿ is standing next to the flowers ＿＿＿ Mary.

e: 倒裝句的動詞須和主要子句的動詞一致，主要子句的動詞為現在式一般動詞，又主詞為單數，故倒裝句用助動詞 does。
q: Louis and his brothers ＿＿＿ playing basketball, and ＿＿＿ Allen. They always play basketball together.

e: 倒裝句的動詞須和主要子句的動詞一致，主要子句的動詞為現在式一般動詞，又主詞為單數，故倒裝句用助動詞 does；而前方為肯定句，故須使用 so，非 neither。
q:
Ann：Do Betty and her roommate Christina go to bed early every night?
Jenny：Yes. Betty goes to bed at 9 p.m., and ＿＿＿.

e: 由後句「我兩個小時前完成了。」可知此處應為肯定附和句。前句時態為現在完成式，且附和句的主詞為 I，故附和句也須用 have。
q:
A：I have finished my homework. How about you?
B：＿＿＿ I finished it two hours ago.

e: 倒裝句的動詞和時態須和主要子句的動詞一致，主要子句的動詞為過去式一般動詞，故倒裝句用過去式助動詞 did。
q:
Jane：Yesterday was Emily’s birthday. Many of her friends went to her birthday party. Did you go there?
Sherry：Yes, I did. I gave her a present, and so ＿＿＿ her two friends.

e: 否定倒裝句用 neither，時態與動詞須與主要子句一致。
q: The math test is difficult. Jane didn’t do well on it, and ＿＿＿ Alex.

e: 倒裝句的動詞須和主要子句的動詞一致，主要子句為被動式且為過去式，故倒裝句動詞為 be 動詞的過去式。
q: Jack was given a watch as a birthday gift, and ＿＿＿ Jeff. They both got a new watch.

e: 倒裝句的動詞須和主要子句的動詞一致，主要子句用助動詞 can，故倒裝句亦為 can。
q: Nancy is good at cooking. She can cook a lot of dishes, and ＿＿＿ her sister, Lucy.

e: 前句為否定句，句尾用either表示否定附和。
q:
A：Can you lend me an eraser?
B：Sorry. I didn’t bring mine, ＿＿＿.

e: 「too... to V」表示「太……以致於無法……」。
q: The water is ＿＿＿ dirty ＿＿＿ drink. Let’s buy some bottled water.

e: 「so… that…」表示「如此……以致於……」。
q: Jack was ＿＿＿ hungry ＿＿＿ he ate two hamburgers.

e: 由 so 之後接形容詞，可知須用 so… that… 的句型，表示「如此……以致於……」。
q: My grandma is so old ＿＿＿ she can hardly stand.

e: 「too... to V」表示「太……以致於無法……」。
q: The bag is too heavy ＿＿＿.

e: 「too… to V」表「太……以致於無法……」。
q: Everyone was ＿＿＿ after the long hike. They didn’t even feel like eating.

e: 「too... to V」表示「太……以致於無法……」。
q: The soup is ＿＿＿ hot for me ＿＿＿ eat.

e: 「too... to V」表示「太……以致於無法……」。
q: Thanks for the cookies, but I am ＿＿＿ anything else.
o: so full that I can eat
too full that I cannot eat

e: so… that… 和 such… that… 皆表示「如此……以致於……」，但 so 後面接形容詞或副詞，such 後面接名詞。
q: The cellphone was ＿＿＿ expensive that I ＿＿＿ buy it.

e: 這裡有許多很酷的玩具。只能從裡面挑出一個真是十分困難。「too… to V」表「太……以致於無法……」。
q: There are a lot of cool toys here. It’s ＿＿＿.
o: so easy that I didn’t try
not hard enough to play with
so hard to pick up one
too hard to choose just one

e: 動詞sings後方須接副詞well。so… that… 的句型，表示「如此……以致於……」。
q: Kelly sings ＿＿＿ ＿＿＿ that she has a lot of fans.

e: so… that… 表「如此……以致於……」。
q: All of the dishes are ＿＿＿ clean that I can even see myself in them.

e: so… that… 和 such… that… 皆表示「如此……以致於……」，但 so 後面接形容詞或副詞，such 後面接名詞。
q: We had ＿＿＿ a good time that we didn’t want to leave.

e: so… that… 和 such… that… 皆表示「如此……以致於……」，但 so 後面接形容詞或副詞，such 後面接名詞。
q: Brenda is ＿＿＿ a smart student that she gets a 100 on almost every test.

e: Bill還不夠高（not tall enough），所以無法搭乘遊樂設施。
q: Bill is ＿＿＿ tall ＿＿＿ to go on the ride. He needs to wait another year or two before he can.

e: 此處須用關係代名詞 that 代替先行詞 website 引導子句。
q:
Irene：Where can I find information about Africa, Lucy?
Lucy：You can ask Jane. She found a useful website ＿＿＿ shares a lot of information about Africa.

e: 關係子句的動詞須與先行詞搭配，先行詞 young women 為第三人稱複數，須用複數動詞。又由 every morning 可知，應使用現在簡單式。
q: Do you know these young women that ＿＿＿ to the park every morning?

e: 先行詞為「物品」時，關代用 which 或 that，且當作主格時不得省略；後方為被動語態，且為過去式，故應為was driven。
q: The car ＿＿＿ stopped right in front of us ＿＿＿ by a strange man.

e: 先行詞為「人」時，關代用 who 或 that，且當作主格時不得省略。
q: The doctors are helping the woman ＿＿＿ ＿＿＿ badly.

e: that 當關係代名詞用，引導形容詞子句：if 當連接詞用，引導名詞子句，表示「是否」。
q: Mr. Huang was the teacher ＿＿＿ shared a lot of knowledge about nature with Terry when he was in junior high school. But Terry is not sure ＿＿＿ Mr. Huang remembers him now.

e: 先行詞為「人」時，關代用 who 或 that，且當作主格時不得省略。
q: Can you believe it? The man ＿＿＿ just passed by us is a world-famous soccer player.

e: 此處須用關係代名詞 that 代替 the house。
q:
Mark：Did Kevin move into the new house his parents bought last month?
Andy：No. He moved into the house ＿＿＿ he lived in before.

e: 「女孩的頭髮」關代用所有格whose。
q: The girl ＿＿＿ hair is short lives next to me.

e: that 當關係代名詞用，引導形容詞子句；where 引導的名詞子句助動詞須接在主詞後面。
q: Alice was the girl ＿＿＿ told me ＿＿＿ find the hotel information at the airport. She helped me a lot.

e: neither 表示「也不」，放句首時後面為倒裝句「Neither＋be 動詞／助動詞＋主詞.」。
q: Jeffery has never been to the USA before. ＿＿＿ have I.

e: 句中的 he has visited 是關係子句，而先行詞是 the places，關係代名詞用 which 或 that。
q: Mr. Wu takes trips a lot. Most of the places ______ he has visited are underdeveloped（低度開發的）countries.

e: 先行詞 the doll 是物品，關係代名詞應用 which 或 that，此處的關係代名詞在形容詞子句中當受格，可以省略。
q:
A：This is the doll ＿＿＿ Jenny dreams of having.
B：We can buy it for her as her birthday gift.

e: never 含否定字意，附和句亦須用否定，而前句動詞是現在式一般動詞，附和句要用助動詞 do。
q: My parents never tell a lie, and ______.

e: A：那個錢包是誰的？ B：我不知道。「不是」Gina 的「就是」Patty 的。 A：好。我們去問他們並找出錢包屬於誰。
q:
A：Whose wallet is that?
B：I don’t know. ______
A：OK. Let’s ask them and find out who it belongs to.
o: It’s not only Gina’s but also Patty’s.

e: 「so did I」表示「我也是」，在此表達肯定附和。
q:
A：I used to sleep late on weekends.
B：______

e: A 說「我不能吃海鮮」，由 B 說「我從不吃它」，可推測 B 會回答「我也不行」。
q:
A：I can’t eat seafood.
B：＿＿＿ I never eat it.

e: 由「我們兩個都應該更用功讀書」可知，B 也沒考好，故用 Neither did I. 表達否定附和。
q:
A：I didn’t get a good grade on this test.
B：＿＿＿ Both of us should study harder.

e: Mike 以前早上常去慢跑。但自從他換工作後，「他一直都太忙，以致於無法那麼做了」。
q: Mike used to go jogging in the morning. But since he changed jobs, ＿＿＿.
o: he has been so busy that he does that
he has been too busy to do that
he has been practicing it hard

e: 由詢問要喝什麼可知，會回答「飲料」。
q:
A：What do you want to drink?
B：＿＿＿
o: It’s sold by one of my relatives.
So do I. Talk to you later.
Either hot coffee or iced tea is OK.

e: 由後句說明「他們生病後決定換工作」可知，Brown 先生和太太兩人過去都常加班。
q: Mr. Brown used to work very late, and ______. However, they decided to change their jobs after they got sick.
o: his family were lonely because of it

e: 由 I like her dishes. 可知，附和句為肯定且主詞為女性。
q:
A：My daughter is good at cooking.
B：＿＿＿ I like her dishes.

e: 由 It can’t be true. 可知，Iris 認為這件事情不可能是真的，Henry 一定是在開玩笑。
q:
Henry：According to the report, eating mud can make people smarter.
Iris：＿＿＿ It can’t be true.
o: You should clean it up with a towel.
I know this is put-down humor.
It’s so real that it hurts my feelings.

e: 由學校失火可知，Fiona 希望神保佑他們並幫助他們度過難關。
q:
Meg：Did you hear the news about a school that was on fire last night?
Fiona：Yes, I did, and ＿＿＿.
o: I think I can borrow money from them
may God bless them and help them through
I should either tidy the classroom or water flowers
there’s mud everywhere at the school

e: 前句問「哥哥是否問過 Erica 此事？」，後句回答 Yes 表示哥哥有問過她。
q:
A：My brother lost his cellphone when he was playing basketball with Erica.
B：Did he ask her about that?
A：Yes. She said ______.
o: he was too shy to ask her
a stranger took it and ran away
he didn’t want to put her down

e: 回答「我也會」，表示前句也是肯定的；用 will 回答，表示前句也用 will。
q:
Ted：＿＿＿

p:
Jack：Hey Andy, did you get enough sleep last night? You look terrible!
Andy：No, I didn’t. Something happened last night that I’ve never experienced before.
Jack：Oh, no. What happened?
Andy：I was sleeping, but then I suddenly woke up and couldn’t move. It was difficult to breathe, and I even thought I saw a monster!
Jack：Sounds like you had sleep paralysis.
Andy：Sleep… what?
Jack：Paralysis. It means you can’t move.
Andy：And this is… normal?
Jack：You’re 22, right?
Andy：Yeah, so?
Jack：That’s an age that many people experience it at.
Andy：So why does it happen?
Jack：Well, when we sleep, we experience Rapid Eye Movement, or REM. It’s called that because our eyes are moving quickly from side to side. It’s the part of the sleep cycle during which the brain is the most active, and so are our eyes.
Andy：Do our eyes really move around like that when we’re sleeping?
Jack：Yes, they do. Also, during this time, our muscles are “turned off” so we don’t try to walk during our sleep and hurt ourselves.
Andy：Wow, I didn’t know that.
Jack：So, usually when we wake up, it’s during the part we are not in REM anymore. But sometimes we wake up when we’re still in REM.
Andy：Oh! So we wake up and want to move, but our muscles are too “sleepy” to move yet!
Jack：That’s right! You got it!
Andy：But what about the monster I saw? It was so scary that I almost died!
Jack：Well, REM sleep is also the part where we have all our dreams.
Andy：So the body wakes up, but the brain is still dreaming?
Jack：Yup.
Andy：This is all very interesting, but also terrifying.
Jack：I can understand that. I’ve had it happen to me a few times, too.
Andy：Really? What did you do?
Jack：I just let it happen and didn’t try to fight it.

Mark Twain is the name of a very famous American writer. The Adventures of Tom Sawyer is a book he wrote, and so is its follow-up, The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn. But did you know that Mark Twain is not even his real name? It’s actually his pen name. There are many interesting facts about Mark Twain. Let’s take a look at a few.
Mark Twain was born on November 30, 1835, as Samuel Langhorne Clemens. He grew up in Missouri, the sixth of seven children. When he was born, a famous comet called Halley’s Comet had just passed by close to the sun. The comet is in an orbit and returns close to Earth about every 75 years.
Before he became a writer, he worked as a boat captain and a miner. He was an inventor, too. He invented a board game! The name by which he became most famous came from his days sailing on the Mississippi River. “Mark twain” means 12 feet of water to sailors.
The American writer was a big fan of science, and so was Nikola Tesla. The two became good friends. He also loved cats. Really loved them. He always said that cats were so much better than people that he’d rather live with them. He often rented cats to keep him company when he traveled and is known to have had 19 cats living with him at one time!
Also, Mark Twain predicted his own death. One year before Halley’s Comet was due to come back, he said “I came in with Halley’s Comet in 1835. It is coming again next year, and I expect to go out with it.” He died on April 21, 1910, one day after the comet had passed by.

p:
Having a sense of humor is something most people think of as being uniquely human. No other living thing “gets” humor. It is so important to us that we can already understand it when we’re just babies. Humor allows us to laugh, and laughing helps build relationships and brings people together.
A sense of humor can bring joy, help us be smarter, healthier, and deal with difficult problems. It can also help us look at things from a different angle and even think outside the box. It can teach us to be playful and not take things so seriously. It can also teach us to laugh at ourselves. People who laugh a lot are not sad or sick very often, neither are those who laugh with them. When the mind is healthy, so is the body.
Children who have a sense of humor seem happier. Those who can appreciate and share humor are also often more sociable and usually have more friends. But most of all, humor can make life really fun. There’s nothing quite like laughing so hard that your stomach hurts or until tears are running down your face.
A sense of humor is not something we’re born with, though. It is something that we learn and grows with us. It also changes when we get older, much like we do. Things that we find funny as kids become too childish to make us laugh when we’re grown up. Babies, for example, don’t really understand humor yet. They just laugh when something we do is funny to them. As children get older, they turn to physical humor and doing funny things either to make themselves or others laugh.
Having a sense of humor is an important part of growing up, and it should be encouraged. Parents should show their kids early on that laughing is fun and that it should be done a lot. Make lots of jokes and tell funny stories. A family that laughs together has lots of fun together!

e: 後句的形容詞子句先行詞為人 the girl，因此第二格的關係代名詞用 who 或 that；Gina 不知道「為什麼」Kevin 沒有邀請他喜歡的女生去派對，因此第一格疑問詞用 why。

q: This Saturday is Emily’s birthday. She thinks ＿＿＿ her dad may take her to Hualien this weekend. However, she is not sure ＿＿＿ her mom will go with them.

e: 由「這個小男孩迷路找不到他媽媽」可知，後句是說他不知道「他能做什麼」。

q: Ben asked his sister ＿＿＿ he should invite the girl ＿＿＿ he met yesterday to go hiking with him.

q: Emily told Ted ＿＿＿ the girl ＿＿＿ stood beside him yesterday was her sister.

B：It was fun! And then we cooked some of the fish ＿＿＿ we caught.

e: 由第一格空格後的介系詞 with，可推知是問跟「誰」去參加派對，且 who引導的名詞子句中的動詞須接在主詞後面；whether 當連接詞用，引導名詞子句，表示「是否」。
q: Teresa wanted to know ＿＿＿ Emily went to the party with last weekend, but she didn’t ask Emily. She asked Linda ＿＿＿ she knew that.

e: 由學生回答在臺南，可知老師問有沒有人知道這個有名的作家在「哪裡」出生。

Teacher：Does anyone know ＿＿＿ the famous writer was born?
Student：I know! It’s Tainan, right?

e: if 引導的名詞子句，動詞時態應與主要子句一致。

q:
A：Could you tell me ＿＿＿ you bought those shoes?
B：The black ones? I got them this evening.

e: how 用來引導名詞子句，表示「如何」；that 當關係代名詞用，引導形容詞子句，在本句可省略。
q: Josh is not sure ＿＿＿ he can finish the report ＿＿＿ his teacher asked him to do.

e: 由語意及文法，可知空格內應填入 whether（是否）。

q: Lucy wants to know ＿＿＿ the boy ＿＿＿ helped her last week will go hiking with her.

q: Learning is like ＿＿＿ a dish. You have to add things a little at a time and not everything at once.

e: 虛主詞為 It，真主詞為 to V。又「打包」在本句為主動用法，故選 to pack。
q: It is not possible ＿＿＿ all these clothes into the suitcase（行李箱）. I need a larger suitcase.

q: I want to know if Nancy ＿＿＿ me with my math homework tomorrow.

e: 根據語意，媽媽要兒子外出前穿上大衣，可知第一格空格為祈使句，而第二格空格則應置入連接詞 or，表「否則」。

q: My pet dog always likes ＿＿＿ with this big towel after I wash her.

e: 本句動詞為 surprised，故空格內應置入 that 來引導子句作為主詞。

q: Rita thinks ＿＿＿ I ＿＿＿ for her is meaningless（無意義的）.

q: It is tiring for Kevin ＿＿＿ eight hours a day.

e:

p:
Wayne：Why are you waving your arms and shouting?
Irene：I’m going mountain climbing with my classmates this weekend. I’m practicing.
Wayne：Practicing for what?
Irene：It is what people should do when they run into a bear.
Wayne：Are you kidding? I think ＿1.＿ people should play dead when they meet one.
Irene：Not really. Hungry bears also eat dead bodies.
Wayne：＿2.＿
Irene：Well, fish is one of bears’ favorite foods. I wonder ＿3.＿ it will work.
Wayne：All right. Then, is starting a fire a good idea?
Irene：I’m not sure. Maybe you can give it a try when you run into a bear.

o: How about climbing up a tree?
How about jumping into the water?
How about running down the stairs?

e:
1. 前句提到他知道很多關於飲食的事，故最有可能寫了一本包含了許多人經驗的書。
2. 由後句文意可知，他相信「他們所吃的食物種類」比吃進體內食物的量「更重要」。
3. 由後句文意可知，他把所有「人們常吃的食物分成兩類」，有益的食物以及有害的食物。
4. 此處解釋為何我們應該遠離糖果、馬鈴薯和白麵粉等食物，故選 why 說明理由。
5. 綜觀全文，可知此句為「無論你是否相信他」。
p:
Do you think that you are overweight? Do you want to lose your beer belly? Or are you thinking of going on a diet? If you are nodding your head, then you must know Michel Montignac because this guy knew a lot about diets. He wrote a book __1.__. It is called The French Diet, and in it, he said people didn’t need to diet to lose weight. He believed __2.__ than how much food they put into their bodies. He put all the foods __3.__, good ones and bad ones. The good foods were the ones that put sugar into the blood more slowly than the bad foods, and they included spaghetti, cereals, and vegetables. What’s more, they stopped the body from storing fat. That’s __4.__ it’s best to stay away from foods like candy, potatoes, and white flour. With Montignac’s way, people didn’t have to exercise very much. His way sounded easy, which was great news to food lovers. However, not everyone agreed with Montignac and his ideas.
__5.__ you believe him or not, here are some healthy ways for dieting. You should stop eating when you are 80% full. Also, you should get lots of fresh food and treat vegetables as the main meal and meat as a side dish. More importantly, enjoy your meal by eating slowly and using it as a time to spend with your family and friends.

p:
Have you ever felt you had to act in a certain way, have a certain look, or do certain things just because of your gender? Many people have thought this way for a long time. Also, these general ideas people have about men and women have affected their roles in society.
In the past, men got an education so that they could find a good job and make money for the family. Because of this, they made all of the decisions for the family, and what they said was final. Besides, men had to be strong, and they were not allowed to show any emotion, especially cry. On the other hand, women usually did not go to school. From their mothers, they learned how to take care of the home. They learned how to keep a good house and be a loving mother and wife. What’s more, women were not allowed to work outside their homes. They were expected to be caring and obedient.
Luckily, for people in this day and age, these old ideas about men and women are changing every day. Now, men can be stay-at-home dads, and women can have high-paying jobs in many different fields. Society is starting to treat everyone equally, and it doesn’t matter if that person is a man or a woman.

The number of fat people in China has increased in the past thirty years. With 300 million overweight grown-ups and 46 million that are obese, the country comes second only to the United States. However, that’s not the worst of it. China’s future is also in trouble because its children are slowing themselves down with lots of extra weight. The study found that 23% of Chinese boys under 20 years old are overweight or obese, while 14% of Chinese girls have the same problem (see Figure 1). 2. 第二段提到 Beethoven 於 1798 年失去聽覺，而第三段提到 Marlee Matlin 是第一位贏得奧斯卡金像獎最佳女主角的聾啞女性，故選 (C)。
3. 第二段提到藝術家 Beethoven 失去聽覺後仍創作出世界名曲 Ninth Symphony，以及和 Vincent van Gogh 齊名的後印象派時期畫家 Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec 的雙腿殘疾、第三段提到聾啞女演員 Marlee Matlin 獲得奧斯卡金像獎肯定，並持續在影視圈交出漂亮成績單，可知沒有什麼事物能阻止這些患有身體殘疾的藝術家追求自我的實現。
p:
Artists make our world more colorful. They sing, dance, make music, and create beautiful things for us to look at and enjoy. It’s not easy to do, and it takes talent as well as a strong body. Just imagine how much more difficult that would be if you had a disability.
One of the most famous artists with a disability was Beethoven. He created the Moonlight Sonata and many more pieces of classical music without being able to hear. In 1798, he had an accident that made him go deaf. However, he never gave up and went on to finish his world-famous Ninth Symphony. Another famous artist was Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec. He was one of the best-known painters of the Post-Impressionist period, along with Vincent van Gogh. At the age of 13 and 14, he broke first his right leg and then his left. His bones did not heal well, and his legs stopped growing. He couldn’t join in many physical activities, so he turned to art, and the rest is history.
Now, artists like Marlee Matlin are showing the world that having a disability shouldn’t stop you from making your dreams happen. She was the first deaf woman to win the Oscar for Best Actress for her role in Children of a Lesser God. She keeps doing great work in both movies and television today. Her parents taught her to “do what you have to do” to get things done, and Matlin and all artists with disabilities are certainly doing that.

3. 由句意可知應填入連接詞 Whether（是否）。Whether 引導子句當主詞時，不可用 If 取代。

e: 感官動詞後面須接原形動詞或現在分詞。
q: The dog jumped up and down happily when it saw a butterfly ＿＿＿ in front of it.

e: 由 called 可知，本句時態為過去式，故 (A)、(B) 不可選。又，感官動詞後面須接原形動詞或現在分詞，故選 (D)。
q: Kevin ______ something ______ and called 119 right away.

e: 花費動詞 spend 後接 V-ing，而 help 後可以接 to V 或原形動詞。
q: The old man was a true giver. Before he passed away, he decided to spend all his money ＿＿＿ hungry people.

e: end up 後用 V-ing 當受詞，而花費動詞 spend 後接 V-ing。
q: Don’t buy that second-hand car. Although it is cheap, you may end up ＿＿＿ more money ＿＿＿ it.

e: 第一句句意為祖父買了一艘船。而 pay 的句型為「pay＋錢＋for＋物」，與題幹不符。第二格的動詞形式受到 spend 影響，須使用 V-ing，因為是人駕駛船，所以不用被動語態。
q: My grandfather ＿＿＿ an old sailing boat, and he now spends most of his free time ＿＿＿.

e: 使役動詞後面接原形動詞，若使用 want，後面須接 to V。第二格後接形容詞，因此用連綴動詞 feel。
q:
I know a few people who always ______ me ______
amazed because they stand by my side each time I feel low.

e: 使役動詞後面接原形動詞，若使用 ask，後面須接 to V。begin 後面可接 V-ing 或 to V，兩者語意大致相同。
q: We’re planning to make a movie that will ______ people begin ______ and think about the problem.

e: 使役動詞 has 後面接原形動詞。
q: Our English teacher has us ＿＿＿ to English news for at least thirty minutes a day.

e: 使役動詞 make 後面接原形動詞，而 help的用法為help＋人＋(to)＋原型動詞，故選 (A)。
q: My mom makes me ＿＿＿ her ＿＿＿ the dishes every night.

e: 使役動詞後面接原形動詞；連綴動詞後面接形容詞。
q: Jerry’s mom makes him ______ his bedroom every week, so his room looks ______.

e: 「使役動詞＋人＋V」表示「叫某人做某事」，選項中只有 ask 與其動詞使用方式搭配正確。
q: On weekends, my parents always ＿＿＿ me ＿＿＿ for hours.

e: 使役動詞後面須接原形動詞。而 taste 在此意為「嘗起來」，其用法為taste＋形容詞，故選 (A)。
q: Oliver put some beef and tomatoes in his soup to make it ＿＿＿ ＿＿＿.

e: 第一個空格由 wait 可知，其後面若接動詞，該動詞須以不定詞形式呈現。第二個空格由 for two years 可知，須用現在完成式，故選 (C)。
q:
A：Your cousin is coming back from Japan tomorrow, right?
B：Yes. I can’t wait ______ her. I ______ her for two years!

e: for 為介系詞，其後方動詞須為動名詞形式；keep 後面若接動詞，該動詞須以動名詞形式呈現，故選 (B)。
q: I am sorry for ______ you ______ for so long.

e: 使役動詞後面須接原形動詞；practice 後面若接動詞，該動詞須以動名詞形式呈現。
q: Mrs. Lee has her son ______ the violin every day.

e: like 之後可接動名詞（V-ing）或不定詞（to V）；而 let 為使役動詞，其後須接原形動詞，故選 (B)。(A) 不符合句意，不可選。
q: My dad likes ______ his car clean, so he doesn’t let us ______ in his car.

e: ask 後面若接動詞，該動詞須以不定詞形式呈現。
q: Sorry, I can’t go out today. I was asked ______ care of my little sister.

e: need 跟 want 後面若接動詞，該動詞須以不定詞形式呈現。
q:
A：I need ______ to the supermarket. Do you want me ______ anything for you?
B：No, thanks.

e: ask 後面接不定詞；practice 後面接動名詞。
q: Amy’s mom asks her ______ ______ English every day, so Amy speaks English well.

e: stop其後若接不定詞，表示「停下目前的事，去做某事」；其後若接動名詞則表示「停止正在做的某事」，依據句意，故選 (C)。
q: You should stop ______ video games now, or you won’t be able to wake up at 6 a.m. tomorrow.

e: enjoy 後面若接動詞，該動詞須以動名詞形式呈現。而第二句話為動名詞當主詞之句型，故選 (C)。
q: My husband enjoys ______. ______ delicious food is easy for him.

e: tell 後面若接動詞，該動詞須以不定詞形式呈現。若為否定用法，只需在 to 前面加 not 即可。
q: Before we entered the glass museum, our teacher told us ＿＿＿ anything in the museum.

e: ask 後須接不定詞；使役動詞 let 後面須接原形動詞。
q: Samantha asked her parents ______ her ______ computer games on weekdays（平日）, but her parents did not agree.

e: ask 後面接不定詞；感官動詞後面接原形動詞或現在分詞。
q: Mandy likes singing. She always asks everybody ______ to her ______, but she doesn’t sing well.

e: 「have＋人＋V」表示「讓某人做某事」。
q: My parents had my brother and me ______ care of the house when they were on a trip to Japan.

e: keep 後面若接動詞，該動詞須以動名詞形式呈現。
q: When Mr. Yang came into the classroom, the students still kept ______. That’s why Mr. Yang was angry.

e: 第一空格是「A＋tell(s)＋B＋not to V...」，第二空格則是用動名詞片語當主詞。
q: Mrs. Wang often tells us ______ to bed late because ______ enough sleep is very important.

e: tell 後須接不定詞，否定用法則在不定詞前面加 not；感官動詞後面接原形動詞或現在分詞。
q: Emma told her sister ______ with knives after seeing her ______ with them. It was dangerous.

e: It is＋adj.＋to V 表「做……很……」，而由句末的 kids，可知逗號後的句子為命令的祈使句，故選 (C)。
q: It is important ______ to the airport on time tomorrow, so ______ to bed earlier today, kids.

e: 由 Brian 要 Nicole別擔心並要她回家休息可知，Brian 會頂替 Nicole 的工作。
q:
Brian：You don’t look good. What’s up?
Nicole：I have a headache. I may not be able to finish the work today.
Brian：Don’t worry. ______ Go home and take a rest.
Nicole：Thanks.
o: Hurry up! I hate to be late.
Now let that be a lesson to you.
I’ll cover for you this afternoon.

e: 由 however 帶出語意轉折，說明即便前方的道路比預期的更漫長、困難，「我們將會一起度過」。
q: The road ahead may be longer and more difficult than we hoped for; however, I believe that ______.
o: we will be scared to death
we will get through it together
we can’t cover for you this time

Son：Mom, may I play basketball after school tomorrow?

Lucy：I’m leaving for the USA for a new job. I’ll miss you.
Ella：I’ll miss you, too. ______ Let’s make a video call with each other every week.
o: Sorry. I didn’t stand by you.

e: 由 Frank 說「這是錯的。」可知，前句應為「Helen，你不應該抄襲我的習作。」。
q:
Frank：Helen, ______. It’s wrong.
Helen：Sorry, but I forgot to do it yesterday.
o: you don’t have to cover for me
I am not able to take your place

e: 由句意判斷，沒聽過父親唱歌是因為他自認「沒有好嗓音」。
q: I’ve never heard my dad sing because he thinks ______.
o: we can’t make him do it
I want him to sound like a star
he doesn’t have a beautiful voice
he enjoys watching a movie at home

e: 由 Ann 詢問與人發生爭執的原因可知，後句應是說明此人推了 Ted 的肩膀並幾乎把他撞倒。
q:
Ann：I saw you fighting with a guy. What happened?
Ted：______ However, I didn’t know who he was.
o: We made a deal to stay good friends forever.
He made me believe that I could win first prize.
He pushed me on my shoulder and almost knocked me down.
He didn’t set sail, so he couldn’t get to where he wanted to go.

e: 由 A 回應閱讀畢業紀念冊總是能讓人想起一些過去的事，可知 B 說明看著畢業紀念冊中的照片時，這些照片喚起了他很多美好的回憶。

A：What are you looking at?
B：The photos in the yearbook. ______
A：I understand. Reading the yearbook always makes people think of something in the past.

e: 由 Andy 說 Wood 老師抓到過他一次，假如他再讓 Adam 抄一次，他也會有麻煩。但是，Peter 接著說 Adam似乎還不曉得老師已發現了；因此 Peter 在對話開頭是說「Adam 問你他是否可以跟你借數學習作。」。
q:
Peter：______
Andy：No way. I won’t let him copy my answers again. Mr. Woods caught me once. If I do that again, I’ll get into trouble, too.
Peter：I think Adam hasn’t known about it yet.

e: 選項中，只有 “When life knocks you down, get back up and fight harder.” 適用於畢業的祝福語，其餘用於「愛情」、「生育」以及「死亡」。

e: 向對方詢問健康的體重數字以及方法，對方回覆可使用相關的工具以及建議加入減重課程，可知「必須要減重來保持健康」。

A：To find out more, you can use the simple tool and join our slim down program.

e: 由後句說有音樂節的活動，可知廣場的群眾是在「看樂團表演」。
q:
A：Why are there a lot of people in the town square?
B：______ There is a music festival.

e: 詢問是否常運動，應回覆「我每天至少跑五英里」。
q:
A：You look healthy. Do you exercise often?
B：Sure. ______

I run at least five miles every day.

e:
1. 信件的內容是由透過印度的飲食習慣來了解這個國家的文化，可推知 Hsing-Chun 也向 Tara 分享過關於臺灣文化的一些資訊。
2. 使役動詞 let 之後接原形動詞。
3. 由動詞 enjoy 可判斷是屬於正向的描述，且後句說明使用左右手的差異，故「這樣讓食物嘗起來更美味」最符合上下文意。
4. 由前一句提到印度當地的麥當勞不販售牛肉、豬肉產品可知，「把乳牛視為神聖的象徵」為原因，「大多數的印度教徒不吃牛」為其結果，故用連接詞 because。
5. 信件的內容主要是介紹印度的飲食文化，不單只是介紹食物本身，信件中沒有提到 Hsing-Chun 對於印度的疑問，語氣上也不是要給 Hsing-Chun 一個教訓。因此是希望 Hsing-Chun 比過去更了解 Tara 的國家。
p:
(Tara, who comes from India, goes to senior high school in Taiwan. She and Hsing-Chun are classmates.)
Hello Hsing-Chun,
I’ve been interested in Taiwan for a long time. Thank you for sharing __1.__, and I’m going to share mine with you through my country’s food.
First of all, not all Indian food is spicy. Don’t let that thought __2.__ you away from trying it. Spices which are used in Indian food are mainly from plants, such as flowers, leaves, fruits, seeds, and roots. In fact, some of them are very sweet.
Second, we Indians enjoy eating our food with our hands and believe __3.__. When eating, only the right hand should be used. In Indian culture, the left hand is considered the dirty hand, and therefore it’s not polite to eat with it. Although it takes time to master the art of bringing food to your mouth with just your fingers, you are just as welcome to eat with a spoon in an Indian restaurant.
What’s more, McDonald’s does not sell beef or pork products in any of their restaurants in India. Around 80% of Indians are Hindus. __4.__ they consider the cow to be a sacred symbol of life, most Hindus do not eat beef, and many are vegetarians. Also, 13% of Indians are Muslims, who eat beef but do not eat pork.
Have you become more interested in Indian food? I hope now __5.__. If you have not tried Indian dishes, it is time to give it a go.
All the best,
Tara
spicy 辛辣的 spice 香料 consider 認爲 master 精熟 sacred神聖的 vegetarian 素食主義者

o: the news about the study abroad program
this makes the food taste better
that’s what we can’t put up with
doing that will get us into trouble
that’s the only way to eat Indian food
you have a better idea of how to cook Indian food
you’ve learned your lesson and will never do that again
you know more about my country than you used to
you understand what I said about the country is true

e:
1. 被動語態說明每分鐘有將近500小時的影片「被上傳」，因為是說明目前的狀況，因此用現在簡單式的被動語態。
2. 用 in fact 來補充說明前句，並提供某種訊息來強調已經說過的某事物。此處說明對於排行榜上都是歌曲以及童謠的現象並不意外，強調音樂具有最高的重複播放性質的這一項「事實」。
3. 由前兩句舉例比較影片類型對播放次數的影響，因此說「這就是為什麼（音樂具有最高的重複播放性質）。」來作結並回扣原因。接著帶出後句，說明「童謠也是按照相同的方式。」。
4. 由表格中的名次以及點閱數，可知 “Despacito” 已不再是 YouTube 歷史上觀看次數最多的影片。2021 年目前第一的是 Baby Shark Dance。
5. 由受歡迎的程度以及其影響力，這首關於鯊魚家族的歌曲「在孩子之間非常熱門」。
p:
YouTube is the second-most visited website in the world, right after its parent company, Google. In 2021, there are over 2 billion YouTube users around the world and more than 500 hours of videos __1.__ to YouTube every minute. YouTube has come a long way and changed the world since its first video, “Me at the zoo,” in April 2005.
•Most watched YouTube videos of all time (2021)
When you look at the most watched videos on YouTube in 2021, you will see every video in the top ten is either a music video or a children’s song. This is not surprising. __2.__, music videos’ replay value is higher than any other type of video. If you watch a video about how a seed becomes a rose, chances are you will only watch it once or maybe twice. On the other hand, if you love a song very much, of course you are going to play it again and again. __3.__ Children’s songs work in the same way.
•“Baby Shark” has reached a new milestone
__4.__ “Baby Shark Dance” has taken its place. “Baby Shark Dance” was made by the South Korean children’s education channel, Pinkfong. The song about a shark family __5.__, and parents everywhere know the power of Baby Shark. What’s more, “Baby Shark Dance” is also one of the most liked and most disliked YouTube videos ever, with more than 30 million likes and 13 million dislikes.
How do you feel about Baby Shark? Do you love it or hate it, and how do your kids feel?
billion 十億 replay value 重複播放性質 milestone 里程碑 education channel 教育頻道 shark 鯊魚 dislike 不喜歡

o: “Despacito” is no longer the most watched video in YouTube history.
“Despacito” has more than 7.5 billion views and is the top music video of 2021.
“Baby Shark Dance” failed to keep its place as the most watched video in YouTube history.
“Despacito” has moved past “Baby Shark Dance” to become the most watched video of all-time.
used to be loved by everyone
has become a hit with children

e:
1. 文中顯示 Johnny 喜歡吃巧克力，第一段倒數第二句又說「Then his mother had no choice but to let Johnny eat…」，表示爺爺帶來 Johnny 喜歡吃的巧克力。
2. want 後須用不定詞「to＋原形動詞」表示。
3. 由後句是向上帝祈求生日禮物的項目，可知他是在睡前「禱告」。
4. have 為使役動詞，後面須接原形動詞。
5. wh- 子句當 hear 的受詞，表示「我所說的」。
p:
Johnny used to have a sweet tooth, and he liked to eat chocolate very much. However, he was not allowed to have any chocolate at home because his mother thought it was bad for his teeth. His grandpa was a kind man, and he loved Johnny very much. Therefore, he usually __1.__ when he visited him. Then his mother had no choice but to let Johnny eat it because she didn’t want __2.__ the old man disappointed. So, Johnny was always happy about his grandpa’s visit.
One evening, a week before Johnny’s seventh birthday, he __3.__ before going to bed. “Dear God, please have my parents __4.__ me a big box of chocolates as my birthday gift next Sunday,” he shouted loudly. His mother heard it in the kitchen, and she went to his bedroom quickly and said, “Don’t be noisy, and you don’t need to shout, either. God can hear you even though you don’t actually speak out.” “I know,” answered smart Johnny with a cunning smile, “but Grandpa has bad hearing. He can’t hear __5.__ in the next room if I am not loud enough.”
disappointed 感到失望的 cunning 狡猾的 hearing 聽力

o: taught Johnny how to brush his teeth
woke up and sat on the bed
spent hours talking to his mom

e:
1. 由文意可知，校長「要學生們去爬」，使役動詞後面接原形動詞。
2. 由文意可知，形容看到學生哭泣，而感官動詞後面接原形動詞或 V-ing。
3. want 後面接的動詞要用 to V 的形式。
4. 由前後文意可知，是說儘管成長的過程會很艱辛，「但這些經驗與回憶會讓你變得更好」。

p:
Animals on the Red List
Animals and plants are a very important part of the environment and are needed for a healthy planet. As a result, it’s very important that we protect them. That’s where the IUCN（國際自然保護聯盟）comes in. It carefully follows wildlife and watches out for possible extinctions. Information on this wildlife is collected and put into what is called the Red List, which has eight levels. The higher a plant or an animal is on the list, the closer to extinction that plant or animal is.
One animal that is high on the Red List is the European hamster（歐洲倉鼠）, which was written about in a new report by the IUCN. They could disappear in the next 30 years. Hamster mothers were recorded as birthing up to 20 babies back in 2016. Now, just 5 years later, they are only birthing 5 or 6. That’s a very big and sudden change. They went from being at the bottom of the list to the top in a very short time. No one can explain why or how this happened, as the reasons behind this change are not yet known. Some scientists say that it could be because of the warming planet, pollution, or even losing their home to farmers.
There are some people who are trying to create some kind of record of the wildlife still on Earth before it’s too late. Some collection that can show the children of the future that those animals really lived on Earth before. One such person is photographer Joel Satore. He hopes that his beautiful and bright photos can teach people about all the amazing wildlife on our planet and get them to become interested in protecting them. He created the Photo Ark, and all his photos can be found on the Internet.

KNSH News
Sorry, the Mona Lisa Is Not Looking at You
By Brian J. Smith January 10, 2024
Have you ever walked into a room with a portrait hanging on the wall, and then felt as if its eyes were following you everywhere you went? If so, you’re not alone. Of course, a portrait’s eyes can’t really be following people around, it just seems that they are. It happens whether you stand to the left or the right of a portrait, and whether you’re close to it or far away. It is such a common feeling, and so many people have had this happen to them that it even has a name, the Mona Lisa Effect（蒙娜麗莎效應）.
If a portrait’s eyes aren’t truly moving inside the painting, then why do we feel as if they are? Some scientists who have studied this effect say that it’s all in our head. Humans have a strong need to feel like they are the center of someone’s attention, even if it’s someone they don’t know or haven’t met. So, does Leonardo da Vinci’s famous painting actually present the Mona Lisa Effect? The answer is quite surprising.
In one study, researchers asked 24 people to look at pictures of the Mona Lisa 26 inches from a computer screen and try to decide which direction her eyes were looking in. They were shown pictures that had been changed in size, had been cropped, or were just a little bit to the right or a little bit to the left on the screen. After 2,000 tests it was shown that she is, in fact, looking to the right at an average angle of 15.4 degrees. This is very important because the Mona Lisa Effect only works if a portrait’s eyes are staring straight ahead. So, although the Mona Lisa Effect may apply to other paintings, sadly, it does not apply to the Mona Lisa herself.

Holi is a two-day Hindu（印度教教徒）festival that is celebrated around the full moon in March. On the night before Holi, people get together and light a large fire. They do this as a way to burn away any angry ghosts that may be around and to show that good always wins. It is a time for people to forget any old problems and start fresh. The next day, people go out on the streets and throw colorful powder at each other. They do it for fun, but also because each color has a special meaning. For example, red is for love, and green is for new beginnings. Some people like to celebrate by throwing water on one another. It’s also common for people to give out candies, sweet cakes, or cookies all through the day. Later in the day, everyone will share a special meal with their families.
Holi has become very popular and is now being celebrated in many countries around the world. Visit India today or enjoy a Holi festival near you!

p:
Most people know what the Olympics（奧運）are. In 2021, they took place in Tokyo, Japan. It’s a sports event that happens every four years. There are summer Olympics, and there are winter Olympics. But did you know that after the Olympics end that there are the Paralympics（帕運）? The word comes from the Greek（希臘語）preposition “para,” meaning “beside.” It means that the Olympics and Paralympics run side-by-side.
The Paralympics are a chance for people with disability or impairment to live out their dreams of becoming athletes. Many such athletes are not able to walk and must use a wheelchair at all times. What choices are there, if any, for these athletes on wheelchairs? Well, actually, as it turns out, quite a lot.
One game in which these athletes can take part in is called wheelchair basketball. It is a team sport that follows almost the same rules as NBA basketball. Of course, because the players are on wheelchairs, the rules are a little different in some places. But the main idea of the game is the same: get points by putting the ball into the basket. Wheelchair basketball is a very interesting sport because the players must use their arms to push their wheelchairs and also throw the ball. Some people even say that it’s a very difficult sport to play.
Another Paralympic sport played on a wheelchair is called Boccia. In this sport, players can be in teams of two, three, or four. There is a white ball called the “jack,” blue balls, and red balls. Players from each team must try to throw their ball as close as possible to the jack as this is how to make points. But Boccia is also a mind game, and players must think carefully about where to throw their balls. Either they can choose to just get their ball close to the jack, or they might want to push the other player’s balls out of the way.

p:
Seeds are found in almost every plant on Earth from flowers to fruits and vegetables. They come in lots of different sizes. They are important for humans because they allow us to plant them into the ground and grow new plants from them. One place near the North Pole（北極圈）thinks that seeds are so important that it had a special building built just to hold them all.
The island of Svalbard is mostly snow, ice, and polar bears. It is as far North as someone can fly to on an airplane. From a snow-covered mountain, a rectangular, gray building called the Svalbard Global Seed Vault can be seen. This building is the only one of its kind and is home to over 1,000,000 kinds of seeds but can actually hold up to 2.5 billion. The Vault is said to be the safest place on Earth for a seed (or a human) to be when the end of the world arrives. It is above sea level, which protects it from any ocean flooding. It is also protected from earthquakes. The room where the seeds are kept is 100 meters into the mountain, and well-protected. The frozen ground keeps the building at -18℃ naturally, easily freezing the seed samples, so they don’t need much power to run it.
The idea behind The Vault is to have a backup for all the foods and crops that are important to humans. If something really bad happens to the Earth one day and all the plants are destroyed, the seeds from the vault can be used to grow them again. The seeds are kept in special packages that will keep them safe. Packages are then put into black boxes, and those black boxes are put on shelves. The seeds will “sleep” for a long time and stay ready to grow at any time.

p:
Below are the pictures and information about ducks and geese and that Helen found on a website.
Ducks
Ducks are usually smaller than geese and have shorter bodies as well as shorter legs. It has been known that ducks only have 16 or fewer bones in their necks. That’s why their necks usually look shorter than those of most geese. As a rule, ducks have long bills that are wide and flat. Like other birds, ducks do not have any teeth. Most species of ducks have orange, green, yellow, black, or white feathers. Ducks live close to bodies of water like rivers, ponds, and lakes. When they swim, they use their webbed feet to help them move through the water. Ducks are omnivores*, which means that they eat basically anything. They are farmed for their eggs, meat, and down feathers.
Geese
Geese are usually larger than ducks and have longer bodies with longer legs. It is also noted that most species of geese can have up to 23 bones in their necks, so they may have much longer necks than ducks. Geese have bills that are shorter and more rounded. Besides, they don’t have teeth at all. What’s more, geese and ducks have very different colors on their bodies. Most geese are gray, black, or white and often covered with different spots. Geese live around bodies of water, and they have webbed feet, too. Geese are known to be herbivores*. They mostly eat grass and other plants. Geese are very popular with farmers for their meat, eggs, and down feathers.
* omnivore - an animal that is able to eat both plants and meat
* herbivore - an animal that eats only plants

p:
Venice Has Its Worst Flood in 50 Years
by Quentin Beck
15 November 2019
Venice, also known as the “City of Water,” is made up of more than 100 islands. The city counts more than 170 canals and 400 bridges, so a lot of people move through the city by boat or on foot, instead of cars. Thanks to its canals, Venice is one of the most beautiful and most visited cities in Italy.
However, Venice experienced its worst flood in half a century on November 12. With strong winds and long waves, the tide rose to 187 cm, and it was the second highest tide that was recorded in the city. The worst flood in Venice’s history was in 1966, with floodwaters reaching 194 cm. The city is often hit by “acqua alta” (high water) in winter time, but a larger problem is the rising sea level. Much of the city was flooded by this year’s acqua alta. The city’s famous St. Mark’s Square, which was one of the lowest parts of the city, was one of the worst hit areas. St. Mark’s Basilica was flooded for the sixth time in 1,200 years－but the fourth in the last 20 years.
Since 2003, Venice has been building 78 large sea gates that can be raised and keep floodwaters out of Venice. The system is called MOSE. Although MOSE was successfully tested for the first time in 2013, it is still not finished. Now, the best guess is that it will be ready by 2025. “I am afraid MOSE will never work, but I have to hope it will,” said Mario Martone, a shopkeeper in Venice. “Or I will have to sell my home and store.”

p:
Have you ever seen anyone surfing? It looks like they are flying across the water on a magic board. One person who knows something about surfing is Bethany Hamilton.
Bethany, who was born in Hawaii in 1990, is not only a surfer but also a sports hero. Both her parents were surfers, and she had them teach her when she was very young. She joined her first competition at the age of eight, and she knew she wanted to be a professional after that. So, she entered more events and even got the company Rip Curl to support her.
However, things changed in 2003. Bethany was bitten by a shark when she was surfing. She lost her left arm, and she was close to death. Although most people would be scared to go back in the water, Bethany was not. Surprisingly, she went surfing again a month after the accident happened. She never lost sight of her goal and kept competing. In 2007, she turned professional, and she won second prize at the Billabong ASP World Junior Championship in Australia two years later.
Bethany has written a book about her experience and called it Soul Surfer, which was turned into a movie in 2011. She is one of the world’s top surfers and an inspiration to all.

p:
In the 1500s, tailors in Genoa, Italy, made really strong pants for sailors to wear. They used a special cloth, so the sailors could wear the pants in bad weather. They were the first jeans. Around the same time, tailors in France made jeans with denim. The cloth was as strong as the one from Genoa.
In the 1850s, Levi Strauss brought denim to the USA. Around 20 years later, Jacob Davis, a tailor, bought denim from Strauss and used it to make pants. Many workers bought them because they were stronger than any cloth out there.
Jeans were expensive in the 1980s. Fashion designers like Gloria Vanderbilt made special jeans with their names on them. Many people wore them because they wanted to be fashionable. Now, people, both young and old, love to have a pair of fashionable jeans. They wear them to be in fashion.

Do you know what language the Navajo speak? They speak Navajo! It is one of the most spoken languages among all the many Native American languages. There are now around 200,000 speakers in the US.
In the past, Navajo was still not a written language, so it was not known by many people outside of the Navajo Nation. That made it the perfect choice to be used as a code during World War II. Besides, there was a special group of Navajos called code talkers. They created and sent coded messages of important plans for the US. The Japanese couldn’t decipher what the messages were about. In fact, they were never able to break the code.
In 2002, a story about these Navajos hit the big screen. The movie was called Windtalkers, and it showed how two Navajo code talkers helped the US successfully defeat Japan.

p:
The Moon Illusion
Have you ever noticed that the full moon looks bigger when it’s near the horizon than when it is high above? ＿1.＿ In fact there are, but the question is: which one is right?
One of the possible reasons that was given by Andrew Vanden Heuvel is the Ebbinghaus illusion. The idea is that two circles of the same size will look different because of the size of the things around them. Take a look at the circles in the picture. ＿2.＿ In this way, maybe the moon looks bigger near the horizon because it’s next to much smaller things, like trees, houses, and buildings. Then when the moon is higher up, it is in the middle of the vast night sky, so it looks much smaller.
＿3.＿ that was given by Andrew is the Ponzo illusion. The idea behind this is that our brains will tell us that something ＿4.＿ larger than it really is when it is closer to the horizon. For example, the two red lines in the picture are the same size, but Line A might look longer because it is closer to the horizon.
In short, there is still a heated debate over the real reason for the moon illusion. As long as you can see the moon in the night sky, it will keep happening.
—Adapted from Ted-Ed: The Moon Illusion by Andrew Vanden Heuvel

3. 內文提到 KFC 於 1970 年代在日本開設第一間餐廳，故可知日本人在那之前尚未吃過 KFC 的炸雞。
p:
【B2L5素養題】
What do people eat at Christmas? For some Japanese people, the answer might be KFC fried chicken and a special cake. This tradition started in the 1970s. At that time, Japanese culture was changing, and people were starting to enjoy western food. KFC opened their first restaurant in Japan then. To let more people in Japan know about their fried chicken, KFC had an idea to sell “Christmas Party Food.” When more KFC restaurants opened in Japan, more and more families would have fried chicken on Christmas Day. Some Japanese people waited long outside the KFC restaurants.
Having a cake for a special day is also a western tradition, and Japanese people followed this tradition around the 1970s, too. However, their Christmas cakes look a little different. You can always see round white cakes with strawberries on top in stores. People like the cake because the white cake and the color of the strawberries look like Japan’s national flag.

p:
【B3L5素養題】
Sarah：Thank you for calling Best Flight. My name is Sarah. How may I help you?
Bruce：Hi, Sarah. Could you please help me? I need to change a flight.
Sarah：Do you have your confirmation number?
Bruce：I do. It’s RT2972.
Sarah：The flight leaves Taipei Taoyuan Airport (TPE) at 5:10 p.m. on June 13 and arrives at Singapore Changi Airport (SIN) at 9:50 p.m. What do we need to change?
Bruce：I have to leave on the 11th and arrive there in the afternoon.
Sarah：I see. Let me check what flights are available. There is a flight at 7:40 a.m. on June 11. You could arrive in Singapore at noon. Would that be okay for you?
Bruce：That should be fine.
Sarah：Right! I’ll book that for you. Because you booked this flight over 48 hours ago, there is a cost to make this change.
Bruce：How much is the change fee?
Sarah：The change fee is $75 dollars.
Bruce：Okay
Sarah：Your new confirmation number is BC2531. Is there anything else I can help you with?
Bruce：No, thank you.
Sarah：Okay, Mr. Wayne. Thank you. Have a nice trip!

p:
【B3L6素養題】
Hiking Life：Mount Hatley
Every year, about 250,000 people from all around the world come to hike Mount Hatley. It is open to hikers from early July to late September because the mountain is usually free of snow during those months.
There are four trails, with different starting points. Hikers usually go to the starting points by bus, then go up on foot. Trail-4 is the most popular hiking trail and the most accessible from the city.
To most hikers, it usually takes two days to go up and down Mount Hatley. They rest at a mountain hut and begin at night in order to reach the summit in time to watch the sunrise.
Staying at one of the mountain huts costs between $50 and $80, and a hot meal is about $8. Also, there are no “free” restrooms on Mount Hatley. It will cost you between $1 and $3 to use the restrooms.
Finally, Mount Hatley is not an easy mountain to hike at all. Please train before your trip. Good luck and happy hiking!

A tsunami（海嘯）is a huge ocean wave. It is the result of earthquakes, landslides（土石流）, or volcanic eruptions（火山爆發）. Tsunami waves are different from regular waves. Even scientists cannot say when a tsunami will happen.

They can grow up to 50 meters high and smash into the coast. The force of a tsunami is very large. It can cause flooding, destroy buildings, and kill people.
Tsunamis are dangerous and powerful. If you can see a tsunami coming, you are already too close to escape from it.

Oxford English Dictionary (OED) often adds new words to the book. Some of these new words are created when two words are put together. One example of this is “voluntourism,” which is made up with “volunteer” and “tourism.” It means you work as a volunteer when you are on a trip. In other words, it is not just to have a vacation. Instead, it is a chance for volunteers to use their skills and interests to help others in need. Every year, many people from rich countries travel to poor countries and hope to do some good. This has been popular for almost half of a century, and it was finally added to the dictionary in 2014.
On the other hand, “staycation” was added to OED in 2010 after it became widely popular in the late 2000s. The earliest use of the word was back in 2003 when a reporter combined “ A ” and “ B ” together. People or families usually stay home and enjoy activities or plan a day trip around their house during their staycation. From swimming in the backyard, visiting a museum, to going to local festivals, these help create the feeling of a vacation without going abroad. After COVID-19 hit the world in 2020, people were not sure if the place they visited was safe. Therefore, the idea of staycation was brought back again.

【B5L4素養題】
Building your vocabulary is one of the key points for mastering a language. However, building vocabulary is more than just knowing words. Here are some right ways to learn words.
First, you should use the words you learn more often. The best way to build vocabulary is to be an active learner. Here are the steps to be one: to learn ten new words every day, to write them down in a diary, and to use them in conversation. When you use as many new words as you can in real life, you can easily memorize them.
Second, it is also good to learn words in small groups. By doing this, you can master a language in a more systematic way. There aren’t really any shortcuts to learning words. To have a wide and large vocabulary, you need time and have to practice in right ways. For example, some roots of English words come from Latin（拉丁）or Greek（希臘）, and to learn these words, it’s better to know how they are formed first. The more you know a word, the better you can memorize and use it.
Third, to build your vocabulary, you should develop a strong feeling which always tells you it is worth doing. Reading out the words or writing them down may sometimes be boring to you, so try to practice them with what you like.

【B5L6素養題】
No matter you are shopping at a supermarket or at a clothing store, many of the prices ＿1.＿ you see usually have something in common. Prices are more likely to end in .99 more than any other pair of numbers. Why aren’t prices just even numbers?
Many stores like to mark their prices to end in .99 for discounts, and customers almost never notice that ＿2.＿. Though no one really knows who or how the trick started, it has been around for at least a century. Ending a price in .99 is based on the theory: we read from left to right, so we usually only see the first number of the price. The price ＿3.＿ starts with a 4 appears to be a better deal than the one that starts with 5. That’s why even though a product for $4.99 may be just one cent cheaper, the trick always helps sell more. ＿4.＿, the .99 alone allows people to believe that the item is on sale. Customers often think they are getting a good deal when they buy something with a price ending in .99.
The trick doesn’t only work for cents. In other studies about women’s clothes, a dress ＿5.＿ price is changed from $34 to $39 is sold more.
