e:
1. 由第三個 Jenny 及 Sam 的回覆可知，是「牛」發出 Moo 的叫聲。
2. one可代替前文提過的單數名詞，在本句中指的是前句的 kangaroos 當中，其中一隻帶著寶寶。
3. 由對話可知，在草地上的有羊群、牛群跟袋鼠們；馬群和獅群則在籠子外。
4. 由對話可知，獅群的籠子大門敞開，加上馬群奔跑，原來獅子跑出門外，動物園裡所有人都忙著逃命。
p:
Jenny：Here we are at the zoo! I’m so excited to come here.
Sam：The weather is nice. We are going to have a lot of fun!
Jenny：Look at the sheep. They are eating grass.
Sam：Hey! Look over here, sheep!
Jenny：Look! There are some cows eating grass, too.
Sam：Moo moo!
Jenny：What are you doing?
Sam：I’m trying to sound like them.
Jenny：Listen! What’s that noise?
Sam：That’s from the elephants. They are big, so they are very loud.
Jenny：What are those hopping around on the grass?
Sam：Those are kangaroos. There is one with a baby. The baby is looking out from the pouch.
Jenny：That’s so cute! I enjoy my time at the zoo. What’s your favorite animal?
Sam：I like lions the most. They are brave.
Jenny：Let’s check out the lions next.
Sam：The lions are not in the cage. Where are they?
Jenny：That’s strange. No one is here, and the gate is open! I have a bad feeling.
Sam：Look! The horses are running away. In fact, all the people are running away!
Jenny：Oh no! The lions got out of the cage. Run!
hop 蹦跳 kangaroo 袋鼠 pouch 育兒袋 cage 籠子

u.q: According to Sam, which animal makes the “moo” sound? according to 根據
What does “one” mean in the reading?
What are those on the grass?
o: They are sheep, cows, and kangaroos.

u.q: What happened in the end?
o: A lot of lions are sunbathing outside their cage. sunbathe 做日光浴
The kangaroos are playing with their babies on the grass.
The lions, the horses, and all the people are running in the zoo.

e:
1. 由前句可知，螞蟻比公牛還強壯，故可推知螞蟻可以移動比自己體重五十倍還重的重量。
2. 由 Susan 的回覆倒數最後兩句話，可推知 Susan 為 Eva 的學校老師。
3. 由 Susan 的回覆可知：只有蟻后才可產卵；螞蟻比公牛還要強壯；螞蟻首次出現在地球上是在 1.4 至 1.68 億年前，故選 (B)。
p:
Q: Mrs. Lynch, which is stronger, an ant or an ox?
Eva
------------------------------------------------------
A: Hi, Eva. It’s a great question. Believe it or not, the ant is stronger. It can lift 50 times its own weight. Ants are insects. They first appeared on the earth between 140 to 168 million years ago. There are three different kinds of ants in an ant nest－the queen, the males, and the workers. The queen is the most important ant of the group. She is very large, and only she can lay eggs. Ants usually build their nest underground, and that is the worker ants’ job. There are many tunnels in the nest, ants use them to get to different rooms. I will tell you more about ants in Thursday’s class. I can show you and the class some videos.
Susan Lynch
weight 體重 nest 窩；巢穴 male 雄性 lay産（蛋） tunnel 坑道

u.q: What does “lift” mean?
What can we know about Susan and Eva?
o: Susan gave Eva a quiz about ants.
Susan might teach Eva science in school.

u.q: Which is true?
o: All the ants can lay eggs.
Ants live in a large group.
An ant is as strong as an ox.
There weren’t any ants 100 million years ago.

2. 由 Amy 說「不要把動物放生進湖裡」及「看到那個標誌嗎？」可知，此處 Amy 最可能會說「那是這裡的規則」。

p:
(Near a lake)
Tom：What are those people doing by the lake?
Amy：Come on. Not again. ＿1.＿ release animals into the lake.
Olivia：Why not? Those fish and turtles will be free soon.
Amy：See the sign? ＿2.＿
Olivia：Don’t worry. They will start their new life.
Tom：Look! There are a lot of dead fish in the water, and some turtles look weak.
Amy：See? What they are doing is wrong!
Olivia：＿3.＿ I won’t do that myself.
------------------------------------------------------
(Ten minutes later)
Tom：Did that happen very often?
Amy：Yes. Many groups release animals here.
Tom：That will lead to ＿4.＿.
Amy：True. The group actions are terrible for the Earth.
Amy：Look! There’s a dying fish. ＿5.＿, give me a hand, ＿5.＿. Let’s save it and set it free.
Tom：No problem.
release 釋放

p:
Mrs. Hu is an English teacher at a high school. Christmas is coming, and she is planning a game, “Secret Santa,” in her class. Here is a note about the game.
Note:
1. Ask every student to fill out a card with their names and hobbies.
2. Put all the cards in a box. Then, every student has to take out a card from the box and find their “lucky person.” Remind students not to tell anyone the names on their card. Also, make sure nobody gets their own card.
3. The game will last for a week. Secret Santa need to give gifts to his or her “lucky person.”
4. Every Secret Santa must leave a clue with every gift.
5. At the end of the week, all the students have to find out their Secret Santa with those clues.
remind 提醒 clue 線索

u.q: What does “Secret Santa” have to do?
o: Give some gifts to a classmate.
Help the teacher with lesson plans.

u.q: What should the students write down on the cards at first?
o: Some notes and key points of the lesson.
The names and hobbies of their Secret Santa.

Sitting on a toilet for over ten minutes may cause rectal prolapse. Then why do people sit on the toilet for so long? There are three reasons. Once they hold off, it will take longer time to wait for the next bowel movement. Lastly, some people like to use cellphones in the restrooms. p:
Mother’s Day is a big holiday. In most countries around the world, Mother’s Day is on the second Sunday in May. However, in many places, people celebrate the holiday at a different time. For example, Spain honors mothers on the first Sunday in May, and France celebrates it on the last Sunday in May. In Egypt, Mother’s Day is on the first day of spring, but in Argentina, it’s on the third Sunday in October.
People also celebrate Mother’s Day in different ways. Most of us usually give our mothers cards, gifts, and flowers. We also take them out to a nice restaurant for lunch or dinner. However, people in Ethiopia celebrate Mother’s Day for three days. Daughters bring their mothers cheese and vegetables, and sons bring meat. Then the mothers cook these things together. After everyone eats the delicious food, they sing and dance. That’s a great way to celebrate Mother’s Day!

2. 由文中可知，參加野餐的有三人；只有 Katie 和 Paul 有帶飲料來野餐；Paul 會在下次教大家做蛋糕，故 (A)、(B)、(D) 皆錯。而在文中第二段則說到「They have a great tea time together.」，故選 (C)。
3. 由文中可知，Bonnie、Katie 和 Paul 在公園野餐，故選項 (A) 的禁止飲食不符合情境；文中的場景在公園，所以不太可能會詢問第一位跑者是誰，故不會選 (B)；Bonnie 和 Katie 及 Paul 是朋友，所以也不太可能會問對方的姓名，故選 (D)。
p:
Today is June 29th. Bonnie goes on a picnic with her friends, Katie and Paul, in the afternoon. In the park, they sit under a big tree and enjoy their afternoon tea. Bonnie brings three hot dogs and a big plate of noodles. Katie shares fresh fruit and juice with everyone. Paul brings some strawberry cake and three bottles of green tea. Everyone loves Paul’s strawberry cake. It is yummy.
They talk with each other and enjoy all the food and drinks. They have a great tea time together. They want to meet again next Sunday for making delicious strawberry cake. Paul will be their teacher.
picnic 野餐 bring 帶 share 分享 fresh 新鮮的

u.q: According to the reading, what is the date of next Sunday? according to 依據
According to the reading, which is right?
o: Four people go on a picnic on the Sunday afternoon.
All the people have a great time together.
Paul will not join them next time.

u.q: Which might be the conversation in the picnic on Sunday? conversation 對話
o: A：Don’t eat or drink here. B：Sorry.
A：Who is the first runner over there? B：Brian.
A：Can I have your name, please? B：Sure. My name is Bonnie Chen.
A：The strawberry cake is great. Can you teach us? B：It’s easy. I can teach you.

3. 由於海報內容各式各樣，有學校、有電影放映和店家的訊息，只有 community center（社區活動中心）最適合，故選 (D)。
p:

B：When does the party start?
A：At 7：00.
B：Um… I can’t go right now. What about I meet you at Li’s at about 7：45?

q: There aren’t ＿＿＿ chairs in the meeting room. More than forty people are coming, but we have only thirty-five here now.

q: Although our car is twenty years old, it still works well. Therefore（因此）, there’s no ＿＿＿ to buy a new one.

q: Tina just bought a liter（公升）of water, but she dropped the bottle on the floor accidentally（意外地）. Now, there is only ＿＿＿ water in the bottle, and there is ＿＿＿ water on the floor.

q:
Ann：＿＿＿ you have a good time at BLACKPINK’s concert（演唱會）tonight?
Rita：Yes. Everyone at the concert was so happy.

q:

Grace：My classmate Tina ＿＿＿.

e: Joseph 今天早上沒吃早餐。他現在很餓。表示否定 eat（吃）的過去式，要用助動詞過去式 didn’t。
q: Joseph ＿＿＿ breakfast this morning. He is very hungry now.

e:
1. 由後方句子可知，他們不是一週只「練習」一次或兩次，而是每天練習好幾個小時。
2. 由第一段第二句可知，奧運每四年舉辦一次，故為 2024、2028 跟 2032 年。
3. (A) 運動員參加奧運不只是獎金，也想為自己的國家贏得獎牌；(B) 倫敦舉辦的是夏季奧運；(C) 由第一段第二、三句可知，許多城市都想主辦奧運。
p:
The Olympics are big events in the world of sports. They take place every four years, and cities around the world want to host them. Thousands of people and athletes come from around the world to be at the games.
The first Summer Olympics was in Athens, Greece, in 1896, and the first Winter Olympics were in Chamonix, France, in 1924. London hosted the Summer Olympics three times—in 1908, 1948, and 2012. Innsbruck, St. Moritz, and Lake Placid hosted the Winter Olympics twice.
The athletes can’t wait to join the Olympics. To get ready for the games, they train hard in their sport for years. They don’t just train once or twice a week. They usually train for many hours every day. They want to win medals and also prize money from their countries.
Olympics 奧運 event 事件 host 主辦 athlete 運動員 medal 獎牌

u.q: What does “train” mean?
When can people see the Summer Olympics?
Which is true?
o: Athletes go to the Olympics just for the money.
London hosted the Winter Olympics three times.
Cities don’t really care about hosting the Olympics.
The Summer Olympics are over one hundred years old.

p:
Sandra didn’t live in a big city. __1.__, she lived in a small, quiet town by the sea. When she was 21 years old, she left to go to college, __2.__. Last summer, she decided to visit her old town and see it for the first time in a long time.
When Sandra arrived at her old town, she couldn’t believe her eyes. __3.__ The main street was really big, and there were many shops on each side of it. There were even new sidewalks, and they were really big, too. A lot of people were walking on the sidewalks. __4.__, many of them were visitors, and they enjoyed the nice weather and checked out the shops. Besides, __5.__. It definitely wasn’t the small, quiet town from Sandra’s childhood.
definitely 肯定地 childhood 童年

because she didn’t like the town

e:
1. 由 Linda 說「她在回臺北的火車上都在睡覺」可知，exhausted 指「筋疲力盡的」。
2. Linda 是在火車上睡覺，不是公車。
3. Mary 原本計畫這週末要去看燈會，但得知燈會昨天已結束而感到驚訝，因為她錯過燈會了。
p:
Mary：Hi, Linda. Where were you yesterday? I called you many times, but you didn’t answer.
Linda：I went to Chiayi to visit my grandparents. Sorry, I forgot to bring my cellphone.
Mary：I see. By the way, there was the Lantern Festival in Chiayi. Did you go see the lanterns?
Linda：Yes, we did. It took us the whole afternoon to see all the lanterns there. After a long walk around the lantern area, I felt “exhausted.” So, I slept on the train all the way back to Taipei. However, I was happy because I saw many creative lanterns and had lots of yummy food.
Mary：Great! In fact, I’m planning to see the lanterns this weekend.
Linda：Too late. March 11 was the last day of the festival.
Mary：Yesterday?
Linda：That’s right.
Mary：Oh my!
Linda：Don’t be sad. I took many pictures of the lanterns. I can show you later.
lantern 燈籠 whole 整個的 creative 有創意的

u.q: What does “exhausted” mean?
What DIDN’T Linda do yesterday?
o: She didn’t sleep on the bus.

u.q: Why did Mary say “Oh my!”?
o: Because Linda didn’t answer her phone call.
Because she is going to see the lanterns this weekend.
Because she missed the Lantern Festival in Chiayi.
Because Linda will show her the pictures of the lanterns.

B：I quit it ＿＿＿ it was boring.

e: 由前後句意可知，A 是在問「為什麼」每個人都笑這麼大聲，故用疑問詞 Why；而 B 的回答，前後兩句為因果關係，前句為果，後句為因，且後接名詞，故用 because of。
q:
A：＿＿＿ did everyone laugh so loudly?
B：They laughed ＿＿＿ a funny joke.

q:
A：You look tired. You need some rest. Why are you still studying?

2. 由後方 even if you don’t want to 可推知 skip 在此應表示「略過」之意，故選 (C)。
3. 全文與 high fever 相關，與圖片相符的選項為 (A)。(B) 為 have a stomachache；(C) 為 broke an arm；(D) 為 have a sore throat。
p:
When you have a high fever, it’s important to take care of yourself. Here are some things you should do and things you shouldn’t do:
Taking care of yourself when you have a high fever helps you get better faster. Follow these tips and rest well!
adult 大人；成人 avoid 避免 activity 活動

u.q: What is the purpose of this reading? purpose 目的
o: To help sick people get better.
To show how to make easy dishes.
To keep people from catching colds.

o: To leave a place suddenly. suddenly 突然地
To not to have or do something.

e:
1. 由第四句作者在候診室等著看醫生可知，他現在在醫院。
2. 由第四到六句可知，作者原本想先休息一下，但因為小男孩的哭聲及男子的講電話聲，他感到生氣，所以他想離開候診室去喝杯溫水。
p:
Last night, I didn’t sleep well because of my blocked nose. This morning, I had a headache, and my throat was sore. I decided to see a doctor. There were a lot of people in the hospital. When I sat in the waiting room and waited for my turn to see the doctor, I tried to close my eyes and take a rest. However, the little boy behind me was crying loudly, and a man next to me was talking on his cellphone in a loud voice. I felt annoyed. When I went to the water cooler to get a cup of warm water, I saw a beautiful nurse with blue eyes and brown hair. She was taking care of a crying kid. She was patient with the kid and was always smiling at him. Soon, the kid stopped crying, and I felt much better, too. Sometimes, a nice person can be my “medicine.” I hope I can be that kind of person in the future.
blocked 塞住的 annoyed 生氣的 water cooler 飲水機 patient 有耐心的

u.q: Where was the writer?
Why did the writer want to leave the waiting room?
o: Because of the noise around him.
Because he wanted to get something to eat.
Because the nurse was calling him.

e: 由圖片可知，男孩「伸手拿」食物。

q:

B：We went to Karen’s party, and we joked about her dress.

q: Ivy wanted to get ______ to work after her child was three, and her husband supported（支持）her as well（也）.

q: I shared the apple pie with three people. I can get a ______.

e: 由去餐廳舉辦派對，可知是在贏得比賽之後或因為贏得比賽，故第一格可用 After 或 Because，但動詞時態皆須用過去式，故選 (A)。
q: ______ the team won the game, they went to a nice restaurant and ______ a big party. Everyone had a good time that evening.

e: 由主要子句可知，Jeremy 成為有名的球員是發生在過去的事情，動詞用過去式。
q: Before Jeremy ＿＿＿ a famous player, he practiced a lot and never gave up. Now he has many fans around the world.

e: 由 because 所引導的子句，可知是在談論過去發生的事，且連接詞 after 須連接兩時態相同的完整子句，故第一格用 ran，第二格用 watched。
q: Lily ______ to her sister’s room last night because she was too afraid after she ______ a horror（恐怖）movie.

e: 由 that is to say（那就是說）可知兩句是相同意思，只是說法不同，在此第一格用 Before，第二格用 because，可同時表達是因為先撞到車才從腳踏車上跌落的。
q: ______ the old man fell off his bike, he hit a car. That is to say, he fell off his bike ______ he hit a car.

e: 由第二句的 be 動詞 was，可知是在講述過去的經驗──邊讀書邊打工。故第一格用 When，第二格用 worked。
q: ______ I was a student, I ______ part-time at a store. It was tiring（令人疲累的）, but I was happy to have that experience.

e: 由首句的前半可知一個過去明確的時間點（十一點半），而在過去某個時間點，進行某動作，使用過去進行式，故選 (A)。
q: It was half past eleven, and I ______ English in my room. I really wanted to sleep, but I couldn’t.

e: a quarter past 表示「……點過 15分」；a quarter to 表示「差 15 分就……點」，故此處可先刪除 (B)、(D)。又，從首句可知時態為過去式，故選 (C)。
q: It was a quarter ______ nine. They ______ about the school music festival in the classroom.

e: 由第二句話，可知首句時態為過去式。人＋hurt，表「（人）傷到……」；連接詞 when 句型，通常用過去簡單式表示進行時間較短的動作，而用過去進行式表示進行時間較長的動作，故第二格為 was taking；第三格由時間副詞 now 可知為現在簡單式，故選 (C)。
q: Regina ______ her back when she ______ a walk. It still ______ a lot now.

e: 由句意可知，洗手「後」才可以幫忙做菜，故選 (D)。
q: Please help me make pancakes ______ you wash your hands.

e: 由 B 回答「我們還有一些時間」，可知現在尚未晚上八點，故選 (D)。
q:
A：Hurry up! The show starts at 8 p.m.
B：Take it easy. It’s only ______. We still have time.

e:
1. 由對話中得知，Susan 當時正在煮飯。
2. Ryan Serhant 成為銷售員是在 2009 年，而他是在 2007 年搬到紐約市。
3. (A) Sell It Like Serhant 是個受歡迎的電視節目。(B) Sell It Like Serhant 的主持人是 Ryan Serhant。(C) 此節目是 Rayan Serhant 主持的節目，不是有關於他的電影。(D) 此節目是教人如何賣東西，而不是教人如何買房。
4. Ryan Serhant在實境秀中短時間內就賣掉許多房屋，還因為該節目而變得有名，更進一步成為另一個節目 Sell It Like Serhant 的主持人，可推知他在實境秀中相當成功。
p:
Tom：Last night, I called you at 7: 30, but you didn’t answer. What were you doing then?
Susan：Oh, I was cooking in the kitchen. Why did you call me?
Tom：I watched the popular TV show Sell It Like Serhant last night. I really loved it and wanted to share it with you.
Susan：What was it about?
Tom：Ryan Serhant, the host of the show, is a successful salesman. He lived in Houston and moved to New York City after he graduated from college in 2007. He wanted to be a world-famous movie star, but his dream didn’t come true.
Susan：What happened after that?
Tom：He found a job and became a salesman in 2009. After that, he joined a reality show and sold many houses in a short time. He became famous because of the reality show, and now he becomes the TV show host of Sell It Like Serhant to teach people to sell everything.
Susan：That’s interesting. I want to watch this TV show, too.
host 主持人 graduate 畢業 college 大學 reality show 實境節目

u.q: What was Susan doing when Tom gave her a call?
What happened before Ryan Serhant became a salesman?
o: He moved to New York City.
He became a TV show host.
He taught people to sell things.
He became a popular and famous movie star.

u.q: Which is true about Sell It Like Serhant?
o: It is not a popular TV show.
The host of it is Ryan Serhant.
It is a movie about Ryan Serhant.
The host of it teaches people to choose a house.

u.q: Which is NOT true about Ryan Serhant?
o: He dreamed of being a movie star before.
He sold many houses in the USA.
He wasn’t very successful in the reality show.

e:
1. 由空格前「停下來！」可知，Adam 阻止了那些小孩，小孩應該就「很快地跑走了」。
2. Adam 騎乘海龜前往海裡的城堡，當他「抵達」時，他很驚訝地喊道：「好漂亮的城堡啊！」。
3. 由前句可知，Adam 享受美食以及觀看海底動物在他身邊跳舞，故 Adam 應「感覺很開心且瘋狂大笑。」
4. 由後句可知，Adam 的臉看起來非常老，且他的頭髮變成灰白色，可知一陣煙「讓他變成了老人」。
p:
Once upon a time, there was a young fisherman named Adam. One day, some children were playing by the sea when they found a turtle. When they started to hurt the turtle, Adam came up and said, “Stop!”
 1.  The turtle was very grateful and said, “Thank you for saving me. Please ride on my back, and I would like to invite you to a wonderful place.” Adam agreed, and they went into the sea soon. When he  2.  the castle under the sea, he was surprised and shouted, “What a nice castle!”
To thank Adam, the king prepared a big meal. He enjoyed the delicious food, and lots of sea animals danced beautifully around him.  3.  All of this made Adam feel like he was dreaming. After some time, Adam began to miss home, and he told the king he wanted to go back. The king said, “I will give you two boxes, but you can only open one. Remember: do not open both!” “OK, I will open only one,” Adam promised. Then a large wave brought him out of the sea.
When Adam got home, he opened the larger box. It was full of gold. “Wow!” he said, “I’m rich now.” Then he thought, “The other box must have something good, too.” He could not wait and opened it. A cloud of smoke  4. . His face looked very old, and his hair turned gray. A deep feeling of regret washed over him, but it was already too late.
turtle 海龜 grateful 感激的 surprised 感到驚訝的 promise 承諾 gold 黃金 regret 懊悔

o: They cheered and clapped for the turtle.
He made the children hurt the poor turtle.
The children looked at Adam and smiled warmly.
He hopped too fast and tripped.
He danced much better this time.
He felt happy and laughed crazily.
He didn’t want to have a meal there.
turned him into an old man

e: 由圖可知，Jerry 昨晚「熬夜寫作業」。

A：Are you playing basketball with your son?

q: Jenny wants to be a famous singer after she finishes college（大學）. So, she starts to take singing classes to make her ＿＿＿ come true.

q: Being a ＿＿＿ again is the last thing Emma will do because she’s sick of making calls, writing e-mail messages, and arranging（安排）meetings for people every day.

e: 由前句「Ken 重感冒」可知，對他來說喝很多水及足夠的休息是「重要的」。
q: Ken caught a serious cold, so it is ＿＿＿ for him to drink a lot of water and get enough rest.

e: 由後句「他的夢想是有一天成為一位男演員」可知，參加演員訓練課程對 Tim 來說是「有趣的」。
q: Joining the actor training program is ＿＿＿ to Tim. His dream is to become an actor one day.

e: Iris 是一位十八歲的「青少年」。她是位專業玩家。她常和朋友們在電競比賽中組隊作戰。
q: Iris is an eighteen-year-old ＿＿＿. She is a pro gamer. She often teams up with her friends in video games.

e: 我們正在製定我們的暑假「計畫」。例如，我們可能會選擇一個新的國家去旅行。
q: We are making ＿＿＿ for our summer vacation. For example, we might choose a new country to visit.

e: 大自然中動物互相「爭鬥」是因為牠們需要食物及想要生存。
q: Animals in nature ＿＿＿ one another because they need food and they want to live.

e: 虛主詞放句首，後面的真主詞常用不定詞 to V。
q: It was important for Emma ＿＿＿ her homework quickly after school because she had to help her parents cook food at the night market.

e: 第一句中缺少 be 動詞，且由 favorites 及第二句的代名詞 them 可知，空格要用複數 be 動詞 are。
q: Taking photos and buying basketball cards ＿＿＿ my favorites. I never get tired of（厭倦）them.

e: want to V 表示「想要……」。
q: I wanted ＿＿＿ beef noodles for dinner, and so did John. That was why we went to a nice restaurant together.

e: 表示「需要……」用「need to V」。
q:
A：You look pale（蒼白的）. What’s wrong?
B：I don’t feel well. I think I need ＿＿＿ a doctor now.

e: not hard 在此不能修飾人，可知本句是以虛主詞 it 代替真主詞 to finish this math homework in just ten minutes 的句型。
q: ＿＿＿ not hard for Diana to finish this math homework in just ten minutes because she is really good at math.

e: 第一個空格，「告訴／要某人要做某動作」的句型為「tell sb to V」，tell 後面的動作以不定詞呈現；第二個空格的句子中，might not be 為主要動詞，但缺少主詞，故此句應以動名詞或不定詞當主詞。
q: It was exciting for Fanny to join the singer training program. Her parents told her ＿＿＿ practicing, and one day, ＿＿＿ a famous singer might not be just a dream.

q: Heidi hates ＿＿＿ a walk at night. She likes ＿＿＿ with her family after dinner.

e: 第一個空格，stop 表「停止某個動作」時，後接動名詞；第二個空格，由前後語意可知，要 Penny 「試著不要」再上學遲到了，應為 Try not to be late，而「Don’t try to…」意思為不要試著去做某些事。
q:
Penny, please stop ＿＿＿ late every morning.
＿＿＿ for school.
o: to get up; Don’t try to be late
to get up; Try not to be late
getting up; Don’t try to be late
getting up; Try not to be late

e: 第一個空格，start 後面可接動名詞或不定詞，另須配合時態，使用過去式；第二個空格，由 is 可知，須用動名詞或不定詞當主詞，故可用 Being 或 To be。
q: My brother ＿＿＿ to be a secretary last month. ＿＿＿ a secretary is his dream job.

e: 由句子中的時間 the day before yesterday 可知，be 動詞要用過去式 was；又「of＋人」通常用於形容「人格特質」，表示 Kevin 人很好。第二個空格，finish 後面接動名詞。
q: It ＿＿＿ Kevin to finish ＿＿＿ the housework for me the day before yesterday.

e:
1. 動詞 like 後面若接另一個動詞，該動詞須以動名詞或不定詞呈現。
2. 此空格應使用過去式動詞，bring 的過去式為 brought。
3. 由空格前後文語意可推知，「因為氣球飛來飛去」，才會讓每個人都很難找到自己的氣球。
4. 空格前面的句子提到，由於氣球飛來飛去，沒人找到自己的氣球。而空格後面的句子提到，當老闆請員工把身邊的氣球拿給氣球的主人時，短短幾分鐘內，每個人都拿到了屬於自己的氣球！因此，可推知空格應為 However，有轉折語意。
5. 此為虛主詞 it 代替真主詞不定詞（to V）開頭的句型，故答案為 it is。
p:
One day, a boss wanted to teach his workers about teamwork. The boss found that the workers liked __1.__ alone instead of working with others. As a result, he __2.__ them into a room with many balloons and asked them to play a game. Each balloon had a worker’s name on it. The workers had to find the balloons with their own names. __3.__, it was hard to find the right one. No one was able to finish this task. __4.__, when the boss asked the workers to give the balloons near them to the owners of the balloons, in just a few minutes, everyone got their own balloons! After this game, the workers learned that __5.__ important to work as a team. The boss was happy to see the result.
teamwork 團隊合作 instead of 而不是 as a result 因此 task 任務 owner 主人 result 結果

o: Because the balloons were in the room
Because the balloons were flying around

e:
1. 對話中提到，人們賺的錢不足以負擔休閒娛樂，所以人們想要用便宜的方式進行娛樂。
2. Jennifer 認為要從夾娃娃機得到獎品很困難。
3. 對話中並沒提到這些商人要關掉夾娃娃機店。
p:
Jennifer：Look! There are so many claw machine stores along this street.
Mike：People in Taiwan really like to play claw machines.
Jennifer：Yeah, but it’s difficult to win a prize. The claw always grazes the prizes before pulling back up. I don’t understand why so many people still play them.
Mike：That’s interesting. It’s never easy to win a prize, but claw machines are everywhere.
Jennifer：That’s right. I learned that there are more than 10,000 claw machine stores in Taiwan.
Mike：Wow, that’s a lot.
Jennifer：True. Many stores closed down because of the weak economy in Taiwan a few years ago, so most of them became claw machine stores.
Mike：No wonder we can see them everywhere now.
Jennifer：Besides, at that time, some people didn’t make enough money for other kinds of entertainment, but they still wanted to relax after work. So, they found a cheaper way to have fun.
Mike：I get it. Every time they played a claw machine, they only spent NT$10.
claw machine 夾娃娃機 claw 爪子 graze 擦過 weak economy 疲軟的經濟 entertainment 娛樂 relax 放鬆

u.q: According to the conversation, what happened after the economy in Taiwan went bad a few years ago? according to 根據 conversation 對話
o: People didn’t want to make money.
People liked to stay home after work all the time.
People didn’t want to spend a lot of money when they wanted to have fun.

u.q: What’s Jennifer’s opinion of the claw machine? opinion 意見
o: It takes a lot of time to play it.
It’s never easy to get a prize from it.
She really wants to open a claw machine store.
Everyone needs to play it for fun.

u.q: According to the conversation, which is NOT true about claw machines?
o: You needed to prepare NT$10, and then you could play one of them.
A lot of people in Taiwan like to play them.
There are over 10,000 claw machine stores in Taiwan.
Many businessmen are planning to close down their claw machine stores.

p:
Dear Manager,
I stayed at your hotel last weekend with my family. When we went to bed, we saw some bugs on the sheets. I killed them, but then we found more bugs on the bed. The next morning, we reported the problem to the front desk staff. She was very nice and gave me another room right away. We moved all our things to the new room. The new one was fine, but we couldn’t sleep well because we were scared there might be bugs on the bed. I think the service at your hotel was good, but the cleanliness needs to improve. I hope you can fix this problem. Thank you for reading this e-mail.
Yours sincerely,
Sara
Dear Sara,
Thank you for your e-mail. I’m sorry for the problems you had during your stay at our hotel. I will talk to all the members of our housekeeping staff to make sure that this never happens again.
As a sign of our apologies, I would like to offer you and your family a free stay in one of our best rooms for three nights. Please let me know if there is anything else I can do for you. Thank you again for telling us about this error. We look forward to seeing you again soon at the hotel.
Best regards,
John Smith
Hotel Manager

Jessie：Daniel, are you free on August 8th? Let’s go to the new museum.
Daniel：No, thanks. I’m not interested in works of art, like paintings.
Jessie：But your favorite actor, Anthony Hopkins, will be there, too.
Daniel：Really? How come?
Jessie：Because his paintings will be on display there from August 1st to October 31st. Besides acting, he’s also good at painting. Didn’t you know?
Daniel：Oh, I didn’t.
Jessie：He said in an interview that Picasso’s style of painting influenced him a lot.
Daniel：No wonder he once played Picasso in the movie. So, you like Hopkins’ paintings, right?
Jessie：Not really. In fact, I’ve never seen his paintings, but I like Picasso’s.
Daniel：I see. Then how will you go to the museum?
Jessie：I plan to take the metro. But if you go with me, I can have a ride in your car.
Daniel：All right. To see my favorite actor, I’ll go with you.
Jessie：Great!

p:
Maria loves to shop for new clothes. When she was a child, her mother often took her to the department store on weekends. Her mother would let her pick out the clothes she liked and try them on. Sometimes, her mother didn’t like them because those clothes were too big for her. She didn’t want Maria to wear clothes in the wrong sizes. For her, the better the clothes fit, the better the person looked in them. Maria keeps what her mother said in mind to this day.
Today, when Maria goes shopping for clothes, she follows the rules her mother told her. If she tries on a skirt and it is too loose, she’ll get the clerk to bring her a smaller one. If the pair of jeans that she is trying on is really long and baggy, she’ll ask her friend to help her find a shorter and tighter pair. For Maria, finding clothes in the perfect size is important, so she doesn’t mind taking a long time to get everything right.
This is the reason why Maria never buys any clothes on the Internet. She wants to be able to see, feel, and try on the clothes before she buys them. If technology ever allows her to do that from her comfortable home, she may give it a try. Until then, she’s more than happy to go shopping for clothes at physical stores.

1. 由全文在描述作者之前養過的寵物狗 Lucy，以及最後一句提到「她真的是我最好的朋友」時，使用過去式 be 動詞 was，推知 Lucy 應該過世了。
2. 由上句可知，They 指「Lucy 的雙眼」。
3. (A) 作者教 Lucy 把戲的時候，她都開心地學，故錯誤；(B) Lucy 在作者最低潮的時刻，從未離開他的身邊，故正確；(C) 作者跟 Lucy 一起做過很多事，也去過很多地方，故錯誤；(D) 作者第一次看到 Lucy 是在家裡客廳，故錯誤。
p:
I really miss my dog. She was the best dog in the world, and there will never be another one like her. My parents surprised me with her on my 13th birthday. I was in the living room when they brought in the biggest box ever. It actually took both of them to carry it. After my parents put it down in front of me, they told me to open it right away because something special was waiting for me inside. When I finally got it open, I saw the biggest, brownest, and cutest pair of eyes looking back at me. They belonged to the sweetest puppy ever, and I didn’t wait for another second to pick her up and hug her.
I looked into her eyes again, and the name Lucy came to my mind. After that, Lucy and I did everything and went everywhere together. I also taught her to do some tricks, and she learned them happily. Lucy was with me during the best times, and she never left my side during the worst times. She was my best friend, and I will miss her forever.

1. 由最後一段可知，作者想要告訴讀者必須正視人類造成的環境破壞，並盡快採取行動。

3. 由第二段可知，有些人爭論建商並不負責，但是有些人認為當地政府才是該被譴責的。
p:
Right before Chinese New Year, a big earthquake hit the south of Taiwan on February 6th, 2016. In Tainan City, a building fell down. Many people died from this. Those people didn’t have enough time to run out of their homes after they felt the building shake. When the neighbors around the building saw that happen, they were so afraid. They couldn’t go back to sleep or let go of the memory. Even worse, there were still lots of people under the building. Even though there were some rescue crews coming from different countries with great tools to help, saving people from the fallen building was not easy at all in this case.
Some said that the house builder should take full responsibility for the event, but some also said it was the local government’s mistake. Whether these points of view are right or wrong, we can’t miss the fact that our damage to the environment also played an important role in it. Soil liquefaction is also thought to be one of the reasons behind the building’s fall. There was so much water in the soil that the ground became weak and couldn’t bear the weight of the buildings on top. As a result, the public are also talking about soil liquefaction now, and they think that the builder and the local government should take responsibility for the building’s fall together.
If we still don’t care about how we’re damaging the environment, nobody knows what’s going to happen next. We should take action to help the environment as soon as possible, or we will be like a really careless student who never learns our lessons.

1. 由第三段的第一句及第二句可知，本段是在介紹美洲原住民製作爆米花的各種方式。
2. 根據倒數第二段，爆米花是因為有了電視而開始流行的，時間大約在 1880 年代以後，至少 100 年以上了，故 (A) 有誤；根據第一段，爆米花是西元前 4700 年就存在的，故 (B) 為正解；根據倒數第二段，1880 年代發明了爆米花機器，故 (C) 有誤；根據第二段，爆米花曾被當作項鍊使用，故 (D) 有誤。
p:
Anyone who has been to the movies knows what popcorn is. It is a delicious treat that has met many people’s need for something natural and full of taste to eat. Popcorn is not a new treat at all. In fact, it has been around since 4700 BC.
The Aztecs made popcorn into things that could be worn around their necks and keep them safe during important events. Later, popcorn was turned into necklaces by Native Americans.
Native Americans also ate popcorn as a meal. To make it, many different ways were used. In one way, the whole ears of corn were put on sticks and cooked over an open fire. In another way, corn kernels were cut down and thrown right into the fire, and only those pieces that happened to pop out of the fire were eaten. In still another way, which was used later, corn kernels were thrown onto the sand that was heated inside a pot. That made more popped corn be collected and eaten.
It wasn’t until the 1880s that the first popcorn machines were made and used in the United States. That made popping corn much easier and popcorn more popular. However, what made popcorn really popular was the TV. Pretty soon, everyone enjoyed having a bowl of popcorn while they watched their favorite programs.
In the early 1980s, microwave popcorn was born into the popcorn family. Now, most people get their favorite popcorn that way, and millions of pounds of popcorn are eaten each year.

p:
Have you ever heard Erchana Murray-Bartlett? She is an Australian runner who finished her 6,300 km (3,900 miles) journey—a marathon every day for 150 days. She broke the world record which was held by Briton Kate Jayden with 106 marathons in 106 days. It’s an amazing achievement. Ms. Murray-Bartlett did it because Australia had many different animals and plants, but some  ? . She wanted to help save these endangered animals and plants and she raised over $100,000 for the Wilderness Society.
It was hard for Ms. Murray-Bartlett from the beginning—she had three injuries in the first three weeks. By the time she ran into Melbourne, her feet swelled a shoe size and she already burned through ten pairs of shoes. “There have been some very difficult days... you’re out there all on your own and you can’t see the finish line and you think, why am I doing this? And during those moments, I think to myself, why,” she told the reporter during an interview. However, she didn’t give up. 1. 全文可分為兩部分：何謂聚光燈效應以及如何克服它。
2. 聚光燈效應指人們高估了他人對自己的觀察和關注程度。選項 (D) 並非聚光燈效應之例子。
p:
Picture that you are walking on the street. Suddenly, you trip. You stand up right away because you think everyone is watching you. Later, you find out that nobody actually noticed. Does this sound familiar to you? If so, you’re not alone.
This is what social psychologists call the spotlight effect. It explained why people always believe many people are watching them. However, people are not paying as much attention to you as they are paying to themselves. The spotlight effect can limit your ability and make you worry too much. Here are some ways to overcome the spotlight effect.
One way is to remember that people are not paying as much attention to you as you think. If you trip or spill something by mistake, chances are that few people actually noticed.
Also, pay attention to others. By doing so, you’ll think more about others and their ideas, not yourself…

p:
Penny hasn’t had the best of luck for some time now. She is tired of being unlucky, so she decided to find out what she can do to change her luck. She goes on the Internet to look for ways to do that, and she finds one possible answer. It says she has to comb her hair inside a church. She isn’t sure how that will change her luck, but she tries it anyway. However, it doesn’t work because bad luck still follows her around. Though the result is not as good as she thinks, she doesn’t give up hope. This time, she asks a friend what he does for good luck. He tells her to find a good luck charm, like a four-leaf clover or a rabbit’s foot, and carry it around with her at all times. She doesn’t know why, but she likes how that idea sounds, so she gives it a try. As luck would have it, Penny finds a coin on the street, so she decided to make it her lucky charm. This turns out to be a bad idea because her luck goes from bad to worse after that.
After all the bad things happen to her, Penny finally stops believing in luck and starts believing in herself. Can you believe it? That’s the moment when her luck begins to change.

p:
Did you know how you could get over 100 hours of your life back? A study from the Royal Society of Public Health (RSPH) found that by just going off social media for one month, you could save 100 hours of your life!
That was the reason for the RSPH to host the activity Scroll Free September. It gives people a chance to give up social media for the whole month of September. By going “scroll free” for a month, people can think about their relationship with social media—what they like and do not like about it, and why they use it. This helps people have a healthier and better relationship with social media.
Besides, the RSPH asked the public what they believe are the most toxic elements of social media. The toxic elements of social media are:
1. The “like” button
2. Push notifications
3. Fear of Missing Out (FOMO)
4. Pressure from influencers

p:
Dear Green Connections,
I love Car Free Day, and I’d like to share how I celebrate it with you and your readers.
Car Free Day is a day that I take very seriously because it is very important not only to us but also to our planet. First, I must tell you that before I found out some facts about this special day, I drove my car everywhere. Sadly, I even drove to places that were less than five minutes away on foot. I now know that was bad. However, all that has changed. On Car Free Day and all the other days of the year, I ride my bike to places I need to go. At first, it was very difficult for me to get to places that were far from my house because I was out of shape and got tired really easily. Then, over time, I got stronger and could travel to spots that were miles away. Now, there isn’t a day that I don’t ride my bike to somewhere nice.
Biking has truly helped me see the world in a whole new way. What’s more, I can’t imagine going back to the life that wasn’t good for me or the environment.
All the best,
Derek

p:
You can do a great deal with money. It can help you in many ways, and you can use it to make many difficult problems go away. With it, you can also buy nice things for yourself and for others. In some cases, it could even save your life. But, give the matter some thought, and you’ll soon understand something important about money: It can’t buy everything. In fact, many of life’s most wonderful things, don’t cost a cent.
Take sleep, for example. Even the richest person on Earth can’t buy a good night’s rest. Of course, you can buy a comfortable bed, but this still doesn’t mean you’ll sleep well. You need to get enough exercise and be in the right state of mind to sleep. If you’re sad, nervous about the next day, or worried about a loved one, not all the money in the world can bring you a natural, sound sleep and sweet dreams.
Another thing money can’t get you—and this is no joke—is laughter. You won’t, after all, see a sense of humor in any department stores or on the Internet. You can’t buy it in any markets or supermarkets, either. It’s a gift from the gods. For, rich or poor, life just isn’t worth living without laughing.
If you think money can buy you love, a happy heart, an open mind, wise friends, family, health, hard work, knowledge, understanding, and life itself, you’re quite crazy, too. In other words, …

p:
Traveling is a great way to see and experience new things in the world. It can be done alone or with friends. Many people who travel often choose the second because it makes traveling more interesting and fun.
Traveling with friends can be easy and free of fights as long as you follow these tips. First, it’s best to discuss what everyone that’s going to be traveling together __1.__ out of the trip. All of you may want to visit Greece for its beaches and old buildings. However, if you’re thinking 10% beaches and 90% old buildings and your friends are thinking the opposite, __2.__. Second, make sure everyone is on the same page about how to travel. You may love staying at hostels and taking buses and trains, but your friends may think those are terrible ideas. Third, __3.__. You’ll have a better trip and more to talk about as long as everyone is allowed to have their own time to do what they want. It pays to be as flexible as you can. Last but not least, communication is very important when traveling with friends. So, bring up problems __4.__ they happen, and don’t be afraid to talk openly and honestly about them. It may be awkward at first, but it will make traveling with friends more enjoyable for everyone.

leaving without your friends is the best way to go
traveling together doesn’t mean doing everything together

2. 由後句提到銳利的牙齒，與足以讓人們想遠離牠們，可知 feared 為「恐懼」。

p:
Sharks have long been feared for their really sharp teeth. Although that is enough to keep most people away from those animals, one part of them that has been received with open arms is their fins. The Chinese eat it in the way of a soup, which they say has many things that are good for people’s health. The dish has even grown to become a sign of wealth and class for them.
For many others, shark fin soup is mean and not needed. The reason for that is how the shark fin is taken. It is called shark-finning, and it cuts the fins off living sharks before throwing them back into the ocean. There, they not only lose blood and die, but they also become food for other sea animals. Shark-finning is threatening the sharks and the oceans because the animals grow slowly and some types are already dying off. Millions of these sea animals die every year, which throws everything off balance.
Lucky for us, governments across the planet have taken action to try to fix this problem. In 2000, the USA made shark-finning illegal. Also, Palau, the Maldives, and the Bahamas have set up natural places that are safe for sharks. Thanks to those actions and others, people have become more aware. More people who are getting married don’t have shark fin soup at their weddings. Also, some restaurants have taken the dish off their menus.
receive 接受 fin 鰭 wealth 財富 blood 血 threaten 威脅 balance 平衡 government 政府 illegal 非法的 aware意識到的

u.q: How do people feel about shark fin soup?
o: The Chinese think it’s a sign of being rich.
Americans love how the fins are taken.
Everybody knows it’s good for your health.
Nobody wants it to be taken off the menu.

u.q: What does something being “feared” mean?
o: It doesn’t make people scared at all.
People are afraid of that thing.

u.q: Which is true about shark-finning?
o: People in the USA won’t get into trouble for doing it.
A large number of sharks die every year because of it.
It doesn’t hurt the animals at all.
It keeps life in the oceans in balance.

p:
Dear friends,
I have some great news to share with all of you. My son just got into one of the top universities in the country. He’s excited, and of course, so am I. There probably isn’t a father in the world who is prouder of his son than I am at the moment. So, I’d like to invite all of you to celebrate this wonderful event at our house. There’s going to be a huge barbecue party with lots of good food and drinks. It will start at around 11:30 on Saturday morning and finish when all the food runs out.
I included a piece of paper with the directions for your convenience. Hope to see you all on Saturday.
Patrick

e:

2. 由 Hans 與 Anne 的評論內容可知，農場在豬的統治、掌權下變得更糟，而在接近故事的結尾，豬的行為變得像人一樣。
3. Vincent 認為此書能讓所有年齡的人都學到一課；Hans 也認為即便孩子、青少年認知程度不同，但都適合閱讀此書。
p:
Goodreads Today
Animal Farm, by George Orwell
Mr. Jones is a mean and lazy farmer. The animals on Manor Farm live badly, and they can’t put up with it anymore. They hope to create a farm where the animals can be equal, free, and happy. However, the farm ends up being worse than it was before. Have you read Animal Farm? What did you think? Tell us!
① Hans says: September 13, 2024
At first, things appear to be going well, but bad things start happening under the rule of two pigs, Snowball and Napoleon. I don’t want to spoil the story for you if you haven’t read the book, so I won’t say much more about it.
I read Animal Farm in senior high school many years ago. It’s a book for all ages. For example, children can read it and just think it’s a fairy tale about animals; however, teenagers will probably get the true message and understand that it’s about power.
② Sabrina says: September 14, 2024
The book is actually very boring. I was asked to read Animal Farm again by my teacher, but I still don’t understand what George Orwell was trying to say here.
③ Vincent says: September 15, 2024
Animal Farm has a great lesson for people of all ages. Take the example of the horse, Boxer, who is a symbol of the working class. He works hard and worries about the farm, but he’s not smart enough to think clearly. He listens to everything the ruler of the farm says. In his mind, that everything Napoleon tells the farm animals is true.
④ Anne says: September 15, 2024
I just added it to my list this month. Near the end of the book, the pigs become more and more like humans. They walk upright, wear clothes, carry whips, and even have a party with humans. The book shows just how power can create dictatorship.
equal 平等 fairy tale 童話故事 upright 直立地 whip 鞭子 dictatorship 獨裁統治

u.q: If Hans “spoils the story” for you, what will he do?
o: Finishing writing a story for you.
Having you read the story he enjoyed.
Telling you what happens in the story.
Sharing his opinions about the story with you.

u.q: From the reading, what can we learn about Animal Farm?
o: The pigs take power and start acting like humans.
The farm gets better and better under the rule of the pigs.
The farmer, Mr. Jones, loves and takes good care of the animals.
Boxer has a mind of his own and a strong head on his shoulders.

u.q: Which is true?
o: Vincent thinks the book is good for all ages, and so does Hans.
Sabrina finally got the true message of the book after reading it again.
Sabrina feels bored with reading the book, and so do the other three readers.
Anne hasn’t finished reading Animal Farm. She’s in the middle of the book.

e: 1. 後面兩句指出兩個年份肉類消耗量變多，因此本句應表示對肉的需求是成長的（growing），故選 (C)。 2. 後面幾句，說明了肉類喜好由牛肉變成豬肉，家禽類也跟著成長，故選 (C)「最受喜愛的肉的名單也有所改變」。 3. 後面句子給了兩個國名—美國與盧森堡，同時指出這兩國人民單人單年消耗肉類的量，故可判斷是詢問選項 (D)「哪一個國家單人消耗掉最多的肉」。
p:
Do you eat meat? Well, if you do, then you might find our next news interesting. A study says that the world has a  1.  need for meat. In 1960, the world ate 64 million tonnes of meat, about 21 kg for each person. In 2007, the number rose to 268 million tonnes, about 40 kg for each person. At the same time,  2. . In the 1960s, beef was high on the menu. Of the meat that was eaten, 40% was beef. In 2007, pork became the star. Poultry also became popular, going up from 12% to 32%, thanks to people’s worries about their health these years. And  3. ? You’re guessing the U.S.A., right? The answer is Luxembourg! In 2007, each Luxembourger ate about 137 kg of meat! Second to Luxembourgers are Americans. In 2007, each American ate about 126 kg! Now, enough with the numbers. I’m playing you a song called Currywurst. The singer sings about his love for the meat dish of the same name. Enjoy!
tonne 公噸 poultry 家禽（肉）
【103教育會考】

o: we have changed our way of cooking meat
new kinds of meat have come on the market
there have been changes in the list of favorite meats
doctors have been worried that we eat too much meat
where does the world’s best meat come from
which country is the world’s biggest meat maker
where can you eat the world’s most delicious meat
which country uses up the most meat for each person

e: 1. 由句尾的 too（也）可以判斷作者也討厭搭公車，但是，文章最後一段卻指出，作者現在變得喜歡搭公車，所以空格應該選 (C)，表示作者是「過去」也討厭搭公車。 2. 前一句指出正在搭公車，本句說明搭公車是要跟朋友見面去看表演，故選 (B) 表示「正要去見面」。 3. 依上下文判斷，作者與 Hui-ting 有數年沒見了，因為此段在描述過去的事情，故選 (D)「過去完成式」。 4. 下一句以現在式表達，可判斷此段在描述現在的狀況，故選 (A)「現在完成式」。
p:
Reader’s Story
It’s never comfortable to take a bus during rush hour on a hot summer day. All my friends hate it. And I…, well, I  1.  it, too.
The story happened two months ago. I was on a bus that was packed with almost everyone in the city. I  2.  my friend Neal to see a show. And then he called and said he couldn’t come. “This is not what I planned for Friday!” I thought. The air on the bus was terrible; the man in front of me smelled like dead fish. While I was feeling sorry for myself, a girl called my name. I didn’t recognize her at first. Then I was surprised to find that she was Hui-ting, my old neighbor. I  3.  Hui-ting in years. We used to play together every day when we were kids. We were happy to see each other, so we decided to have dinner together. And that was the start of many dinners after.
With Hui-ting, the bus ride  4.  something I love. The bus is still packed with people, but I enjoy the ride every day.
(Xiang Chang, Taipei)
rush hour 尖峰時間 recognize 認出
【103教育會考】

e: 1. 由信件第二句 give a party at our new house（在新家辦個派對）可判斷 Angelica 邀請朋友的目的是參觀她的新家。 2. B、C、D 的房子都在路的盡頭的河邊，關鍵句為 Walk past the tree, take the first right turn.（過了樹第一條路右轉），故選 (D)。
p:
My dear friends,
My family and I moved into our country house one month ago. The kids are planning to give a party at our new house. I hope all of you can come. The party will begin at 11：00 a.m. on Saturday. There will be lots of food and drinks.
Together with this letter is a map to our house. After you get off the train, take the road in front of the station. Follow it and you’ll see a chicken farm. Don’t make any turns. Keep going and you’ll see a bridge. Cross the bridge and there will be a big tree on you left. Walk past the tree, take the first right turn, and then walk for five more minutes. You’ll see several houses. My house is at the end of the road, next to the river.
Angelica
【103教育會考】

u.q: Why did Angelica invite her friends?
Look at the map. Where does Angelica live?

e: 選項 (A)「他的朋友認為他是個很棒的舞者。」對話中只說有上舞蹈課，沒說是個好舞者；選項 (B)「他跟 Cecilia 在上烘焙課。」對話中只有說上舞蹈課，沒說上烘焙課；選項 (C)「他的朋友不喜歡他做的衣服。」與倒數第二個 Gloria 所述相符；選項 (D)「他不知道如何跟朋友說不。」未在對話中提及。故本題選 (C)。 2. 從第二個 Gloria 對話可知，Gloria 不想去 Eddie 的品嘗會。故選 (D)。 3. 由對話可知，Cecilia 與 Gloria 都不喜歡 Eddie 的烘焙，之前是由 Gloria 戳破 Eddie 做衣服的夢，所以這次 Gloria 希望由 Cecilia 來戳破 Eddie 的烘焙夢，由此判斷句中的 it 是指告知 Eddie 關於他的（爛）烘焙，故選 (A)。
p:
Cecilia：Eddie’s having a tasting party this Saturday.
Gloria：No!
Cecilia：And we’re both invited.
Gloria：No! I told you I’d never go to any of his tasting parties again!
Cecilia：He said he wanted to share his newest cakes with his dearest friends.
Gloria：If he sees us as his dearest friends, he should stop having tasting parties!
Cecilia：Well, looks like baking really brings joy to his life.
Gloria：But it takes joy away from mine! Last time I was in bed for three days after his party.
Cecilia：If you hate it so much, you can just tell him.
Gloria：Why do I always have to be the bad person? Remember when I woke him up from his dream of making clothes? There was a lot of crying, and he wouldn’t talk to me for moment. You do it this time.
Cecilia：I can’t. How am I going to face him in our dancing classes if I tell him?
Gloria：So we still have to lie at his party again?
Cecilia：I’m afraid so.
【103教育會考】

u.q: What can we learn about Eddie?
o: His friends think he is a great dancer.
He is taking baking classes with Cecilia.
His friends did not like the clothes he made.
He did not know how to say no to his friends.

u.q: Which is true?
o: Cecilia has not talked to Eddie for a month.
Cecilia had a good time at Eddie’s last party.
Gloria shared Eddie’s cakes with other friends.
Gloria does not want to go to Eddie’s tasting party.

u.q: What does it mean?
o: Tell Eddie to stop telling lies.
Tell Eddie how to find joy in baking.
Tell Eddie to stop crying over small things.

e: 1. 由 wear white all the time（成天穿白色的）與 People kept coming in and asked for our help because they got hurt.（人不停的湧入尋求我們的幫助，因為他們受傷了。）可判斷 Josie 在醫院工作。故選 (B)。 2. 選項 (A)「她因為受傷所以聖誕節沒有上班。」由文中可知，十二月二十五日 Josie 有上班；選項 (B)「她不喜歡 Howell 在午餐時間的聊天內容。」由一月三日的內容可知，Josie 是不喜歡 Howell 午餐時的說話內容；選項 (C)「當校車被卡車撞時，她失去了她的兒子。」由十二月十五日的內容可知，是別人失去孩子，不是Josie；選項 (D)「她喜歡 Lonnie參加聖誕派對的服裝點子。」由十二月二十二日的內容可知，Josie 覺得 Lonnie 的點子不好。故本題選 (B)。 3. 由十二月三十一日最後一句話的內容可判斷，Clarke 警官並不同意那年輕男子的說法，故選 (D)。而選項 (A)、(B)、(C) 的內容均未在筆記本上提到。
p:
（Below is what Josie wrote in her notebook.）
Dec. 15
A very sad day. A school bus was hit by a truck. Many kids were badly hurt. A little boy lost his life. His mom was the kids’ teacher. We couldn’t bring her back, either.
Dec. 22
Lonnie said she’ll wear all white to the Christmas party. I said she’s lost her mind. We wear white all the time. Who would still want to wear white on Christmas Eve?
Dec. 25
People kept coming in and asked for our help because they got hurt. Why do people always do stupid things on holidays?
Dec. 31
The police brought in a young man who broke his leg when he was trying to enter a house. When taking car of his leg, I asked him why he wanted to enter another person’s house, and he said he just wanted to borrow a pot. But Officer Clarke said he’s been borrowing many pots from strangers’ houses.
Jan. 3
I knew my lunchtime was over when Howell came to my table. He’s a nice guy. But how many heads he’s cut open is the last thing I’d want to know when I’m eating beef sandwiches.
【103教育會考】

u.q: Where does Josie work?
Which is true about Josie?
o: She did not work on Christmas because she got hurt.
She does not like what Howell talks about at lunchtime.
She lost her little boy when the school bus was hit by a truck.
She liked Lonnie’s idea about what to wear for the Christmas party.

u.q: What do we know from the reading?
o: The truck driver who hit the school bus died.
Howell loves to have beef sandwiches for lunch.
Lonnie did not want to go to the Christmas party with Josie.
Officer Clarke did not think what the young man said was true.

e: 1. 文中主要提到 Nathan Lang 何時（in the 1970s）開始他的演藝生涯、哪部片讓他成名（Young Hours）、何時（in the 1980s）開始不再受歡迎等。與選項 (C)「Nathan Lang 演藝生涯的起落」敘述最相符，故選之。 2. 下一句即補充說明 swoon over 的現象，Women wanted a husband like him; men wanted a brother like him.（女人想要一個像他的丈夫；男人想要一個像他的兄弟。），表示人們為 Nathan Lang 瘋狂。故本題選 (B)。 3. 第一段最後兩句說明電影 Dreams 的狀況：Nathan Lang 演得好而得獎、但票房不佳。與選項 (C)「……電影裡 Nathan Lang 不再是個演員，而是那可憐的老人。然而，好的演技不總是票房的保證……」相符，故選之。
p:
GNB News
Forever Takes a Bow
Actor Nathan Lang, 78 years old, died in his sleep last night in his house. Nathan Lang started his acting life in the 1970s. He was most known for playing Justin Maud in Young Hours. The movie made the world swoon over him. Women wanted a husband like him; men wanted a brother like him. Forever Justin, his fans called him. After Young Hours, Nathan Lang was seen in several big movies： Fallen, After Tonight, and Killing Jules. The last one won him a best actor award. In the 1980s, Nathan Lang lost his shine on the big screen. During this time, his movies never entered the top 20 list. Nathan Lang’s last movie was Dreams. Though the movie won him two best actor awards, it did not bring his fans back to the theater.
This Saturday morning, 10 o’clock at St. Peter’s Church, there will be a “movie party,” as Lang wished. Friends and family will get together and enjoy once again the good times he brought to the world.
award 獎項
【103教育會考】

u.q: What is this reading mostly about?
o: Nathan Lang’s love and hate for his family.
The good and bad about Nathan Lang’s movies.
The rise and fall of Nathan Lang in show business.
Nathan Lang’s life before and after he became an actor.

u.q: What does swoon over mean in the reading?
Here are reviews about Nathan Lang’s movies. From the reading, which is most likely a review for Dreams? review 評論 likely 可能
o: …nothing new in the story; Nathan Lang clearly didn’t do enough homework about his part in the movie. It was no surprise that the movie didn’t make it into the top 10 list the first week it was out…
…it became Nathan Lang’s second best-selling movie and also this year’s third best-selling movie in the country and may even get him another best actor award…
…see him not as the actor Nathan Lang anymore but as the poor old man in the movie. However, good acting does not always help with the ticket sales…

…the story is fresh and interesting, but the acting is not. However, it has been the country’s best-selling movie for the past three weeks. Clearly Nathan Lang’s fans cared less about his acting than his handsome face…

e: 1. 由 ③ Duckland： The only city staying in our top three for five years,…（鴨市：唯一連續五年保持在前三名的城市，……）可知，這城市排行榜報告不只辦了兩年，故選 (D)。 2. 選項 (A)「今年前五名中的一座城市在東方。」由第 ⑥ 點可知，第四名的牛市是東方的城市，與敘述相符；選項 (B)「很少人去牛市做生意。」由第 ④ 點可知，牛市是商業城市，故不符；選項 (C)「北方沒有城市進入今年的前十名。」第五名的獅市是北方的城市，故不符；選項 (D)「鵝市是動物島第二大城市。」排行榜中未提到。故本題選 (A)。 3. 文中可判斷的訊息有：Goosetown 去年第二名、Tigerville 去年第一名、Duckland 去年第三名、Turtleland 去年沒有進榜、Cowtown 去年第七名，這五項訊息相符的只有選項 (D)。
p:
（Here is this year’s report on the Top Ten Cities of Animal Island by Best Living.Com.）
① Goosetown：Climbing up from last year’s second place, Goosetown comes in first for its lovely parks, cultural centers, and comfortable living space.
② Tigerville：Losing its top place to Goosetown, Tigerville is still a beautiful city, and as green as ever.
③ Duckland：The only city staying in our top three for five years, Duckland is now cleaning itself up for next year’s Football World Cup.
④ Oxtown：Not just a famous business city, Oxtown has turned itself into a garden city.
⑤ Lionville：Famous for its culture and beautiful gardens, Lionville is the first city in the north to enter our top five.
⑥ Sharkville：With winter sports as good as Oxtown’s, this exciting city is our second best pick in the east.
⑦ Foxland：This city with white beaches could rise higher in the rankings if there were fewer traffic problems.
⑧ Goatville：Dropping two places, Goatville should now think more about parks than shopping centers.
⑨ Turtleland：New in our top ten, this old fishing town is full of surprises.
⑩ Cowtown：Dropping from number seven, Cowtown must clean up the air.
culture(-al) 文化（的） ranking 排名
【103教育會考】

u.q: Which is NOT true about the report?
o: It tells us what some cities are known for.
It tells us what some cities need to deal with.
Green space plays an important part in the report.
It is the second year that Best Living.Com did the report.

u.q: What can we learn about the cities in the report?
o: One city in this year’s top five is in the east.
Few people come to Oxtown to do business.
No city in the north entered this year’s top ten.
Goosetown is Animal Island’s second biggest city.

u.q: Which is the most likely ranking of LAST year’s top ten cities of Animal Island? likely 可能
o: ① Tigerville ② Goosetown ③ Cowtown ④ Oxtown ⑤ Duckland ⑥ Goatville ⑦ Lionville ⑧ Sharkville ⑨ Foxland ⑩ Turtleland
① Tigerville ② Goosetown ③ Duckland ④ Beartown ⑤ Lionville ⑥ Sharkville ⑦ Goatville ⑧ Cowtown ⑨ Foxland ⑩ Oxtown
① Goosetown ② Tigerville ③ Duckland ④ Foxland ⑤ Beartown ⑥ Goatville ⑦ Cowtown ⑧ Lionville ⑨ Oxtown ⑩ Sharkville

e: 1. 選項 (A)「所有人都說屋頂花園的好話。」六個受訪人中，Samuel 並沒有說好話，故不符；選項 (B)「有些人收錢協助蓋屋頂花園。」只說讓人欣然出錢，並未說有付錢讓人協助，故不符；選項 (C)「所有人都在蓋屋頂花園之前談論過它。」並未在訪談中提及，故不符；選項 (D)「有些人執行蓋屋頂花園的計畫。」由六人訪談中可明確知道 Jasmine 與 Wilber 是執行計畫的人，與敘述相符。故本題選 (D)。 2. 選項 (A)「它讓公寓裡人們更靠近。」符合 Jasmine 說的話；選項 (B)「它利用落在公寓頂上的雨水。」未在訪問中提到；選項 (C)「它讓公寓在夏季成為較舒適的地方。」符合 Rosie 說的話；選項 (D)「它給公寓裡的人們機會種自己的食物。」符合 Flora 說的話。故本題選 (B)。 3. 由 at first（起先；開始時）可判斷 Wilber 指的是蓋屋頂花園這件事情，再由 Wilber 所承接的 Jasmine 訪談內容可得知，他們的確花了點力氣 trying to make them understand why it’s good to build a garden on the roof（試著讓他們的鄰居理解為何在屋頂蓋花園是件好事），故選 (C)。選項 (A)、(B)、(D) 並未在整個訪談中提到。
p:
（Six people are being interviewed about the garden on the roof of their building.）
Jasmine：I loved the idea when Wilber first told me about it. We had lots of meetings with our neighbors, trying to make them understand why it’s good to build a garden on the roof. Now people love coming here, and it’s helped many of us become friends!
Wilber：The whole thing wasn’t easy at first. But Jasmine helped a lot. And she was really good at making people happy to give money for the roof garden.
David：My kids love going up there. They sit there watching butterflies and birds. The roof garden brings them closer to nature.
Samuel：You want something green? Visit the park! It’s only one block away! After the roof garden was built, bugs started flying into my apartment! And the kids leave mud on the stairs when they come down from the roof!
Rosie：Our building is now cooler in the summer. My baby sleeps well even on hot summer days!
Flora：Guess where these tomatoes are from! Not from the supermarket. They’re from our roof! Isn’t that wonderful?
roof 屋頂
【103教育會考】

u.q: What do we know about the six people in the interview?
o: They all said good things about the roof garden.
Some of them were paid to help build the roof garden.
They all talked about the roof garden before it was built.
Some of them worked on the plan to build the roof garden.

u.q: Which of the good things about the roof garden is NOT talked about in the interview?
o: It brings people in the building closer together.
It uses the rainwater that falls on the top of the building.
It makes the building a more comfortable place during summer.
It gives people in the building a chance to grow their own food.

u.q: What does the whole thing mean in the interview?
o: Having meetings at the roof garden.
Taking care of the roof garden every day.
Having people agree to the idea of the roof garden.
Inviting people to make more use of the roof garden.

e: 牆上（on the wall）有兩個方形，故選 (D)。
q:
Look at the picture. The girl drew two ＿＿＿ on the wall.
【104教育會考】

e: always smile（保持微笑）與 remember to say “Welcome” and “Please”（記得說「歡迎光臨」和「請」）等，均是服務生（waiters）的基本「禮貌（politeness）」，故選 (B)。
q: The waiters are asked to be ＿＿＿; they should always smile and remember to say “Welcome” and “Please.”【104教育會考】

e: 主要子句的 is pretty（是美麗的），與附屬子句的 does not look good（看起來並不好看），有語意上的轉折、反差，故選 (B)。
q: This dress is pretty, ＿＿＿ it does not look good on me.

e: 本題考附加問句。主要句子中動詞為 is，而動名詞 Getting up 為主詞，於附加問句中應改為代名詞 it，故選 (D)。
q: Getting up early on a cold morning is not easy, ＿＿＿?【104教育會考】

e: 以 until 連接的時間子句中，用現在簡單式來描述將來的事情，故選 (A)。
q: Tonight I’ll stay at a office until I ＿＿＿ the work.【104教育會考】

e: 「spend＋時間 / 金錢＋V-ing」表「花了……時間 / 金錢做某件事」，故選 (B)。
q: Charles ＿＿＿ a day in the department store looking for a hat for his wife.【104教育會考】

e: over the past two months 表「過去到現在這兩個月期間內」，再從第二句 now 可判斷，前一句在講述「一件事情持續至今」，故選 (B)。
q: Tom ＿＿＿ ten pounds over the past two months. He looks much thinner now.【104教育會考】

e: one ＝ a watch，代替前面「已提過、未指定」的單數可數名詞，而「other＋複數可數名詞」、「another＋單數可數名詞」，故選 (D)。
q: I don’t like any one of these three watches. Can you show me ＿＿＿ one?【104教育會考】

e: 關鍵詞 can’t wait to see her （等不及要見她）表示前述事情尚未發生，但即將發生，故選 (D)。
q: On Children’s Day, Ms. Lee, a famous storybook writer, ＿＿＿ to Molly’s Bookstore to talk about her new book. My two little kids can’t wait to see her.【104教育會考】

e: when 用來引導兩件同時發生的事情。由上下文可知，when 引導的附屬子句缺過去簡單式動詞 appeared (at Katie’s party)，寫作時為避免重複，可以過去簡單式助動詞 did 代替，故選 (D)。
q: No one thought James would appear at Katie’s party. So when he ＿＿＿, everyone was surprised and could not believe their eyes.【104教育會考】

e: 第二句出現過去時間點 2010 年。由上下文可知，第一句「B&J Café 成為城中最高建築」這件事情發生在第二句「O&G飯店成為（城中）最高建築」之前，須用過去完成式表示，故選 (B)。
q: B&J Café ＿＿＿ known as the tallest building in town. However, O&G Restaurant became the tallest building in 2010.【104教育會考】

e: be famous for… 表「以……聞名」，而關係代名詞於關係子句中當受格時可以省略，故選 (D)。
q: Actor David Piper became tired of talking about the movie ＿＿＿ after he was interviewed about it many times.【104教育會考】

e:
1. 寫作中，通常以下一句來補充說明本句的意思。文中的下一句「舉例 （Like…）」說明「上午晴天，正午卻下大雨」，表示天氣變化大（changed a lot）。故選 (C)。
2. 寫作中，冒號後面通常為補充說明。文中冒號後面的句子為條件句 If the weather is nice,… 可判斷，Aunt Lisa 接下來要講的是計畫：根據天氣好、壞，要帶 Mary 去不同的地方。故選 (A)。
3. And 之前，描述了若天氣好時（If the weather is nice,…）要去的地方，所以 And 之後應該就是天氣不好時要去不會弄濕身體的地方（without getting wet）。故選 (B)。
p:
From：Lisa Clyne (lisaclyne@mail.com)
To：Mary Faber (maryfaber@mail.com)
Date：Thursday, April 2, 2015
Subject：Welcome
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Dear Mary,
Uncle Billy and I are excited about your visit.
The weather has ＿1.＿ these days. Like today, it was sunny in the morning, but rained heavily at noon. So we’ve＿2.＿： If the weather is nice, I’m going to take you to Smith Farm. They’re having a special horse show this week. I’m sure you’ll like it. And ＿3.＿. We can go shopping at Mimi’s Department Store; there we can walk around without getting wet. Rain or shine, we hope you will have a good time here.
See you tomorrow at the train station at 9：00 a.m.
Love,
Aunt Lisa【104教育會考】

o: worried about your trip to here
decided to take you to a nice place
we all love animals very much
don’t forget to check the weather

e:
1. 由下面幾句的解釋，可判斷這顆行星離地球真的很遙遠，要花上千萬年才能飛抵該星球（take more than 12 million years to get there），根本算不上近鄰（neighbor），故選 (A)。
2. 寫作中，冒號後面通常為補充說明。由冒號後面敘述，這星球又熱（1000℃）又下玻璃雨（glass rain），生命不可能存活（life is not possible），可判斷這顆星球除了顏色，其他條件與地球完全不同。故選 (C)。
3. Even so（即便如此）為轉折語氣，表示此段應該是描述找到這顆行星的好處。再由最後一關鍵詞 a good start（好的開始），可判斷，寫作者認為，找到這顆行星的同時，也帶來了希望。故選 (A)。
p:
NEWS HUNT
Kieran Hardy 11/07/2013
For years, we thought our Earth was the only blue dot up there. Now another has been found. Its name is HD189773b. HD189773b is an exoplanet, a planet outside our Solar System, and is one of the nearest exoplanets to Earth. Even so, ＿1.＿. Here’s why： It is 63 light years away. That means it is 370,440,000,000,000 miles from us. Even if we fly at 3,500 miles an hour, it will take more than 12 million years to get there.
＿2.＿：It is much bigger, it is made of gas and it is burning hot. In heat as great as 1,000°C, life is not possible. What is worse, it rains glass. If 1,000°C does not kill you, glass rain will.
Even so, finding this blue giant ＿3.＿. It is the first time that we have been able to see the color of an exoplanet. The color of a planet gives us ideas about what is happening on it. While we have a long way to go before we find a new planet to live on, finding a blue dot is a good start.
exoplanet 系外行星 Solar System 太陽系
【104教育會考】

o: we cannot really call it a neighbor
we do not know anything about it yet
we might not be able to stay there for long
we are not sure how long it takes to get there
What’s more, it is not water that makes HD189773b look blue
With its blue color, HD189773b could be a second Earth for us
Except for its blue color, HD189773b is nothing like our home planet
Because of its blue color, people guess there might be life on HD189773b
helps us know more about Earth

e:
1. 關鍵句為 Anna 的前兩句：Anna 的母親與姐姐們都是「醫生（doctors）」，而她確定自己「將會（I will...）」盡可能的遠離醫院，可判斷 Anna 被問的問題應該是跟自己的將來（future）有關。故選 (A)。 2. 選項 (A) 的 Lily 選擇的是販售衣服（selling clothes），並未提她擅長製衣（making clothes），故不符；選項 (B) 的 Bill 只有提到父母親養了許多寵物（kept lots of pets），並未提父母職業，故不符；選項 (C) 的 Ryan 有提喜歡網上交友（making friends online），相符；選項 (D) 的 Anna 並未提自己曾經住院很常一段時間，故不符。故本題選 (C)。
3. them 代替前一句提到的 Those stories。故選 (C)。
p:
Below is how four students answered their teacher’s question in class.
Lily：I like shopping and talking to people. I think I can learn how to do business. Maybe selling clothes is a good business for me.
Ryan：My hobbies are playing computer games and making friends online. We often share our funny stories by e-mail. I guess I will learn more about computers and make super-smart computer programs.
Bill：My parents have kept lots of pets since I was little. We’ve experienced many things together, good and bad, happy and sad. Those stories have always stayed in my mind. One day, I will share them with people by drawing and writing books.
Anna：Though my mom and two sisters are all doctors, I’m sure I will stay as far away from a hospital as I can. I hate being sick, and I’m afraid of seeing sick people looking weak and sad. I’ll keep strong by playing my favorite sport, tennis, every day. One day I’ll join the national team and be another Lu Yen-Hsun.
【104教育會考】

u.q: What question did the teacher most likely ask in class? likely 可能
o: “What do you want to do in the future?”
“What’s your plan for the coming vacation?”
“What do you like to talk about with your friends?”
“What’s your favorite thing to do with your family?”

u.q: What do we know from the reading?
o: Lily is good at making clothes.
One of Bill’s parents is an animal doctor.
Ryan enjoys meeting people on the Internet.
Anna was once very sick and stayed in the hospital for a long time.

u.q: What does them mean?

e:
1. 第二段描述 Nick Foster 的父親很會做菜，再加上最後一句 “A family needs only one good cook（一個家庭只需要一個好廚子）” 可判斷，第一段與第二段應該是反差，用來描述 Foster 的母親不會做菜（cannot cook well）。故選 (B)。
2. 選項 (A)「Foster 如何開了自己的餐廳」、(B)「Foster 的父親何時與其母親結婚」、選項 (D)「Foster 如何從其父親學到了做菜的藝術」均未提。但第三段有說他的確從母親那學到關於做菜的一件事情—No experiments, no experience.，故選 (C)。
p:
Here is the preface of Nick Foster’s new book Married to Food.
Preface
My mother was lousy at cooking. To her, cooking was more like an exciting experiment. You put some of this and some of that in a pot, and you wait and see what will happen. “No experiments, no experiences.” is what she would say when her experiment did not turn out good, and I heard that a lot.
My father was a good cook, and he loved to cook, too. He often said that he got my mother to marry him with a table of delicious food, not with a beautiful ring. “A family needs only one good cook,” he said.
Now I am a cook myself. And I have my own restaurant. I learned how to cook from my father, of course. From him, I learned the art of cooking. But I did learn one thing from my mother. It’s her famous saying： “No experiments, no experiences.”
preface 前言 experiment 實驗
【104教育會考】

u.q: What does it mean when someone is lousy at something?
o: They are not interested in it.

u.q: What can we learn from the preface?
o: How Foster started his own restaurant.
When Foster’s father married Foster’s mother.
What Foster’s mother taught him about cooking.
How Foster learned the art of cooking from his father.

e:
1. 走一步，走二步，走三步，走四步。Anna 取完三張卡後的位置在 Gate Watchdog；Kate 取完三張卡後的位置也在 Gate Watchdog；Billy 取完三張卡後成功抵達 Dreamland；Ivan 取完三張卡後的位置在 Candy House。故選 (C)。
2. 選項 (A)「沒有人能從 Lion King 開始」，因為每抵達 Lion King 時就必須倒退三步，故相符；選項 (B)「卡片可以用來決定誰先開始」、選項 (D)「卡片可以用來決定從哪裡開始遊戲」，由上方敘述可知，卡片只能決定走幾步，故不符；選項 (C)「沒有人能在第一輪走到 Light Church」，因為抽到可以走四步抵達 Golden Bear ，到那裏就可以直接走到 Light Church，故不符。故本題選 (A)。
p:
Here are the rules for a game called “Trip to Dreamland.”
1. Each player begins at START.
2. In each turn, first take one of the four cards to decide how many spaces to move： for one space, for two spaces, for three spaces, and for four spaces. Then follow the words next to the , if there is a at the place you arrive at.
3. The first one who gets to Dreamland wins the game.
turn 回合 space 步、格
【104教育會考】

u.q: Below are the cards which four kids have taken since they began the game. Who has won the game?
What can we learn about the game?
o: One can never begin his turn from Lion King.
The cards can be used to decide who goes first.
One can never get to Light Church at the first turn.
The cards can be used to decide where to start the game.

e:
1. 第一段第三句「水在你的每日生活中有多重要」結論了第一句「一年會在你腦海出現一、二次（hit you once or twice a year）的想法（The idea）」。故選 (A)。
2. 文章第一段引導讀者感受水的重要，第二段為重點，說明了水在 Tanzania 這類缺水國家對女性一生的影響—花越多時間取水（More time spent collecting water），就越少時間受教育（less time for learning），也因此越難脫離貧困（With less time spent at school, their chances of getting well-paid jobs are small），如此惡性循環著。故選 (C)「水如何影響著一個人的未來」。
3. 第二段With less time spent at school, their chances of getting well-paid jobs are small… 的 their 指 girls’ ，與選項 (B) 內容相符，故選之。
4. 第二段第一、二句指出，Tanzania 取水工作落在女性肩上（the job of collecting water falls on women’s shoulders.）尤其是女孩（Girls are often kept from school to collect water while their brothers stay at school studying.）。因此，若這四個國家狀況一樣，那應該選擇女孩取水時數普遍遠高於男孩的圖，故選 (D)。
p:
The idea may hit you once or twice a year. You come home on a hot summer day, hoping to have a cool bath, and find out there is no water. Then you see how important water is in your everyday life. However, in many parts of the world, water is not just about one’s everyday needs.
In countries like Tanzania, water is hard to get, and the job of collecting water falls on women’s shoulders. Girls are often kept home from school to collect water while their brothers stay at school studying. Studies show Tanzanian girls who live 15 minutes from clean water spend 12% more time at school than those who live an hour away. More time spent collecting water means less time for learning. For these girls, “Knowledge is power” is not just words; it is a sad fact in real life. With less time spent at school, their chances of getting well-paid jobs are small, and they often have no voice in important matters, like who to marry. These girls are often married into poor families. They have little money or knowledge to take care of their children, who often end up dying young. For the baby girls who are lucky enough to live, their life may still center around “water,” just like it did for their mothers.
【104教育會考】

u.q: What does The idea mean in the reading?
o: Water is important in one’s everyday life.
Water is not just about one’s everyday needs.
It is nice to have a cool bath on a hot summer day.
We should not take a bath when there is little water.

u.q: What is the reading mostly about?
o: Why it is important to save water.
How water may give a country power.
How water may play a part in one’s future.
Why it is hard to get water in poor countries.

u.q: What do we know from the reading?
o: Children in poor countries die from drinking dirty water every day.
Girls who spend little time at school have a harder life when they grow up.
Girls in countries like Tanzania are often paid less for the same job than the boys are.
Children from poor families are often kept from school to take care of younger children.

u.q: Families in the countries of Benin, Ghana, Guinea and Madagascar deal with the job of water-collecting the same way Tanzanian families do. From the reading, which chart best shows the fact? chart 圖表

e:
1. 第二個 Amber 第一句「For Liz’s birthday cake! （拿蛋糕）」 說明了 Garden House 為 bakery，故選 (A)。
2. 倒數第二個 Keith 與 Amber 可知 Keith 打了數個電話給 Amber（why didn’t you answer my calls），不知道 Amber 電話沒電了（My cellphone is dead!）。故選 (C)。
3. 第三個 Amber 說明了語音留言內容：Amber 與 Matt 一起吃午餐，所以兩人會直接從餐廳去慶生會，因此要 Keith 下班後幫忙去取蛋糕。只有選項 (A) 相符。
p:
(At Liz’s birthday party)
Amber：Don’t tell me you didn’t go to Garden House.
Keith：Why would I go there?
Amber：For Liz’s birthday cake! I left you a voice message this morning!
Keith：But you said Matt would go to the bakery! And why did you come here without me? I was waiting outside your apartment for an hour!
Amber：No! I said I’d have lunch with Matt, and we’d come straight here from the restaurant. So I asked you to help get the cake after work.
Keith：No, you did not! And why didn’t you answer my calls?
Amber：My cellphone is dead! I said in the message that you could call Matt’s number if you wanted to find me. Now please tell me you did bring the gift we got for Liz.
Keith：What gift? I’m sure you didn’t say anything about a gift in the message.
Amber：I told you that yesterday!
message 留言
【104教育會考】

u.q: What is Garden House?
What can we learn about Keith?
o: He forgot to meet Amber and Matt for lunch.
He did not know how to get to Amber’s apartment.
He called Amber without knowing her phone was not working.
He did not know Amber left him a voice message this morning.

u.q: Which sentence was most likely part of the message that Amber left Keith this morning? likely 可能
o: “Matt and I will go to the party after lunch.”
“Don’t forget to buy a birthday gift for Liz.”
“You can go straight to the party from your office.”
“I need to talk to you about the party this weekend.”

e:
1. 第三段 Froggie 選擇忽略水溫緩緩升高（getting warmer and warmer）的環境改變，導致最後的死亡（And he never woke up）指出了本故事的寓意，與選項 (C) 「人們對於緩慢惡化的問題視而不見」最接近，故選之。
2. 選項 (A)「他學會與他人分享自己喜歡的事物」、選項 (C)「他有次差點因為水蛇而失去一個摯友」和本句 There’s no water snake trying to eat me and I can have this place all to myself! 不符；選項 (D)「為了熱水浴，他想回去同樣的鍋內」和本句 Froggie went back to the same kitchen, totally forgetting he had been there 不符。選項 (B)「他以為他的願望成真」與 Froggie knew it was his dream pond. What he didn’t know was... 相符，故選之。
p:
Froggie was a frog who never remembered where he had been. His biggest dream was to find the best pond to swim freely without worrying about water snakes. One day, Froggie hopped to a kitchen and jumped into a pot full of hot water. Froggie felt the burning heat and hurried out of the water as fast as his legs could carry him. “I almost died there!” Froggie thought.
A few days later, Froggie went back to the same kitchen, totally forgetting he had been there. He again hopped into the same pot. This time, the water inside was cool. He looked around and thought, “There’s no water snake trying to eat me and I can have this place all to myself!” At that moment, Froggie knew it was his dream pond. What he didn’t know was that the water was warming up over a low heat.
After thirty minutes of swimming, Froggie felt the water was warmer but he thought of this as a nice surprise. “This sure is the best place for swimming. I get to have a hot bath, too.” During his comfortable bath, the water kept getting warmer and warmer. Froggie was so comfortable that he fell asleep. And he never woke up.
【104教育會考】

u.q: What lesson can we learn from Froggie’s story?
o: Life is too short; one should live it to the fullest.
Those who use their time well will win in the end.
People are blind to problems that slowly get worse over time.
It is difficult to give up old habits, but easy to pick up new ones.

u.q: What do we know about Froggie?
o: He learned to share what he liked with others.
He thought what he had hoped for became real.
He once almost lost a dear friend to a water snake.
He wanted to go back to the same pot for a hot bath.

e:
1. 第一段說明上教堂的人數逐年減少，第二段接著指出另一個問題—錢（there is also the problem with money），可判斷 calamitous state 應該與問題、麻煩（trouble）有關，故選 (A)。
2. 選項 (A)「1980 到 2005 年之間，幾乎沒有五十歲以下的人上教堂」，由圖表 2 可知，2005 年之前上教堂年齡平均值仍在五十歲以下，故不符；選項 (B)「2010 年，五十歲以下上教堂的人只佔總人數百分之六」，由兩張圖表均看不出來，故不符；選項 (C)「2020 年，上教堂人數的百分比會掉到 1980 年的一半以下」，由圖表 1 看，1980年百分比為 11，2020 年預測為 4.4 ，故相符；選項 (D)「1980到 2020 年間，長者上教堂的人數上升，導致教堂年齡層老化」，由第一段的最後一句可知主因是年輕人變少，故不符。故選 (C)。
3. 僅有選項 (C)「關閉的教堂下場如何」在第三段提到：變成 restaurants、school gyms、nightclubs（夜店），甚至 knocked down（拆除），故選 (C)。
4. 報導最後一段為結論，當中的 the church 是泛指所有教堂，而本篇文章從頭到尾都在說教堂邁入老化與沒落，甚至關閉，因此與選項 (D)「報導中的十五個國家，有些國家，像是 Denmark，上教堂的人數百分比低於十；其他的國家，像是 Poland，則高於百分之七十」後半段所描述有高百分比人口上教堂的現象不符，故選 (D)。
p:
The Metro Times
Oct. 1. 2020
These years churches are in a calamitous state. To start with, the number of church-goers is dropping sharply (see Figure 1). Many say they do not belong to any church, and those who do go less often than they used to. Going to church appears less and less on people’s to-do list. Another worrying fact is that fewer and fewer young people go to church, which leads to an older church (see Figure 2).
And there is also the problem with money. Keeping a church door open is not cheap. Fewer people going to church means little money coming in. This makes it harder to keep a church open.
When the time comes for a church to close, there is little to do but to sell it. Churches that were lucky enough to find a buyer were put to other uses. Some were changed into restaurants or school gyms, and some even became nightclubs, for example. Churches that had little luck were knocked down in the end.
Just like a store that keeps losing business needs to think of ways to save itself, it is perhaps time for the church to try to win people’s hearts back and play an important part in people’s lives again. This is not something that one can simply pray to get an answer to.
figure 圖 average 平均
【104教育會考】

In 2020, the percentage (%) of church-goers drops to lower than half that in 1980.
